articles.title: British heavyweight Moses Itauma stretchered out after shock defeat in gruelling world title fight
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic shatters Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appears to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight world-title contest in London.
articles.body: Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar."He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said. "From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.Hrgovic - wearing the red and white checks of his country - made his entrance first to a wall of boos, before the mood inside the O2 Arena flipped as Itauma emerged to a huge roar - taking his time and soaking up the reception.The crowd had made its allegiances clear after a fiery build-up which included Itauma shoving Hrgovic, the Zagreb man slapping him back and plenty of verbal sparring.Itauma came out with real intent, landing straight lefts from his southpaw stance. Hrgovic is known for his durability but struggled to keep pace with the Briton's speed early on.Early in the second, a right hook knocked Hrgovic off-balance and his glove touched the canvas. Oasis star Noel Gallagher and boxing legend Prince Naseem Hamed were among those watching as the crowd gasped at almost every Itauma punch, whether it landed or not.But by the end of the third, Itauma - who had boxed just 26 professional rounds before his first world-title fight - was already breathing heavily.There had also been questions over his chin, simply because it had never really been tested. Hrgovic began landing the occasional heavy shot but Itauma took them well and fired straight back.A fight in the crowd momentarily took attention away from the action in the fifth before an Itauma uppercut in the closing seconds brought the focus back to the ring.Itauma continued to fire combinations but Hrgovic was barely budging. A huge right landed on the bell in the sixth and another followed in the seventh, yet the Croatian simply walked through them.The Briton was well ahead but, rather than box his way towards victory, he continued to chase the knockout. A flurry in the eighth backed Hrgovic on to the ropes and had him in trouble, but Itauma was grimacing between exchanges and looking increasingly spent.By now the danger was clear. Hrgovic came out with renewed purpose in the ninth and landed a thudding right which sent Itauma staggering backwards, almost through the ropes.The youngster somehow stayed upright but his legs had gone. Hrgovic continued to press and when Itauma slumped into his corner, exhausted and barely able to defend himself, referee Howard Foster waved off the contest as the towel came in.Hrgovic admitted he had been "outboxed" but leaves London as Croatia's first heavyweight world champion, with Frank Sanchez waiting as the IBF mandatory challenger.A unification fight could follow, with Daniel Dubois holding the WBO title and set to face Fabio Wardley again in October.For Itauma, this was supposed to be a coronation.Instead, he leaves the O2 Arena with questions over whether the step up came too soon.He has time to rebuild and there will be a strong feeling that, with a little more experience, this night could have ended very differently.Londoner Dubois was stopped by Joe Joyce as an unbeaten 23-year-old before going on to become a two-time world champion. Itauma has even more time on his side."He's an amazing fighter," Hrgovic said. "I am the present. He is definitely the future."Promoter Frank Warren suggested Itauma was carrying a leg injury in the final round but backed him to return."Moses gave everything," he added. "He has to go back to the drawing board and he can come again."The expectation around Itauma will not disappear entirely overnight but the aura of invincibility has gone.

articles.title: Mount Fuji pics, life-changing ramen and a weak yen - why young Brits are going to Japan
articles.summary: Photos of Mount Fuji, bowls of ramen and the bustle of Shibuya Crossing are filling up social media feeds.
articles.body: Mount Fuji pics, life-changing ramen and a weak yen - why young Brits are going to JapanImage source, Maitri SanghviImage caption, Seeing others' holiday snaps of Japan on social media made Maitri Sanghvi want to go thereAs I open up Instagram, I see another person in their late-20s has been to Japan.It shouldn't come as a surprise any more."I cannot scroll through TikTok or Instagram without seeing videos of people in [convenience store] 7-11 and trying all the different skincare and trying all the snacks and the viral sandwiches and the viral drinks and going to all the viral restaurants," says Alex Baker, who has been to Japan three times.There's been growing hype about Japan as a travel destination among young British people.Data from the Japanese National Tourism Organization, external shows that 483,157 British tourists visited Japan in 2025, up 24.8% on 2024 and up 40.8% on 2019, the benchmark year used by travel companies to compare with pre-pandemic trends. Provisional data for 2026 suggests numbers are continuing to grow.This reflects the boom in total tourism to Japan since the pandemic, with a record number of foreign visitors in 2025.The Brits in their 20s and 30s I spoke to gave a long list of reasons for wanting to go to Japan - the cityscapes, food, anime, nature, history, gaming, temples. But they largely agreed that social media was the main driving force behind so many young people heading there.When Maitri Sanghvi scrolled through TikTok, "Japan just kept popping up," she says.It was a big reason why Maitri, 24, and her boyfriend went for three weeks earlier this year. "Seeing [Japan] on social media restarted my urge of wanting to go," she says.Search #japantravel on TikTok or Instagram and you'll see countless videos of Mount Fuji, bowls of steaming ramen, itinerary suggestions, small villages in the Japanese Alps, the Fushimi Inari torii gates in Kyoto, the neon lights of Osaka's Dotonbori, and the chaos of Shibuya Crossing."Seeing other people's Japan videos definitely influenced my decision to go," says Aden Ibrahim, 29.Image source, Aden IbrahimImage caption, Aden says the social media buzz around Japan made him want to goSince he went with friends last July, Aden has posted dozens of TikToks of his trip, and he's still uploading them more than a year later. One captioned "Japan made it out the group chat" has 1.1 million views.Travelling to Japan isn't cheap - return off-peak flights with a layover in China start at about £450 with a budget airline. But the yen is weakening, making it cheaper for tourists when they're actually out there - even as rising prices hit residents. In July, the yen fell to a 40-year low."You can literally get a bowl of life-changing ramen for £3/£4 compared to a rubbish one here for like £20," says Faye Jawad, 26, who reviews restaurants on TikTok and visited Japan last year.Image source, Faye JawadImage caption, Faye says eating out in Japan was surprisingly affordable"When the yen was weakening, I thought 'actually this is a good time to go, things are going to be cheap'," says Vivek Haria, 26, who has a trip planned for this autumn. His interest in Japanese culture means he's wanted to visit for years - he has been learning the language and even sings in the UK-Japan Choir - but he says the value of the yen made it even more attractive.The low prices have led to many tourists splashing out on souvenirs when they're out there. Videos of people showing off their Japan "haul" of flavoured KitKats, stationery and clothes have become popular on social media.When Sam Corbett, 23, was in Japan in May he bought so many souvenirs - including snacks, matcha, clothes and skincare - that he had to buy an extra suitcase, which he stuffed full. Everything was "really affordable," he says.Image source, Yuichi Yamazaki/AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, Many visitors talk about being entranced by Japan's convenience stores Almost all the Brits I spoke to had stuck to the same route known as the Golden Route: Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, often with day trips to nearby destinations like Nara, Hiroshima and Mount Fuji.It's easy to see why so many tourists pick this route. These cities are easy to travel between and packed with some of Japan's biggest attractions.But complaints about badly-behaved tourists are sparking debate about overtourism.Chiyuki Izumii, a tour guide for the Japan Guide Agency, feels tourist behaviour has got worse in recent years. She says that while her customers are respectful, she's seen other tourists jumping queues for buses, blocking space on board with big suitcases, carving their initials on trees in Kyoto's bamboo forest, speaking in loud voices at night and entering restricted areas to take pictures. Some authorities are cracking down. Fujikawaguchiko, a town near Mount Fuji, cancelled this year's cherry blossom festival after repeated issues with misbehaving tourists, while Tokyo's Shibuya ward, home to the famous Shibuya Crossing, started issuing on-the-spot fines for littering in June.In July, Japan increased its international tourist tax, external - typically incorporated into flight and boat tickets for people leaving Japan - from 1,000 yen (£4.60) to 3,000 yen, which it says will be spent on things like improving public transport and restoring historic sites.Image source, Shawn Goldberg/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty ImagesImage caption, Overtourism is a big topic of discussion in cities like KyotoSome visitors were surprised just how crowded major cities in Japan were."I was prepared for it to be busy but I didn't expect it to be as busy as it was," says Millie Dring, a huge anime fan who went in November with a friend to celebrate her 21st birthday. The DisneySea theme park near Tokyo was so busy that Millie and her friend only went on one ride, which had a three-hour queue, and felt overwhelmed by the crowds.Image source, Millie DringImage caption, Millie says cities like Tokyo were even busier than she expectedSam blames some of the crowds at tourist hotspots on social media hype and he says he regrets going to some places just because they were popular online. One dessert spot he went to in Kyoto after seeing it "all over social media" was very busy "and there wasn't a single local person in the queue," he says.Sites like the Hakone torii gates and Arashiyama bamboo forest had huge crowds of people trying to get Instagram-perfect photos, he says.But for some visitors, the hustle and bustle of the tourist destinations are all part of the attraction."I think there's a snobbiness around being a tourist over the past couple of years where people want to avoid looking like one," says Laura McGregor, 29, who's spending two weeks in Tokyo and Osaka in November for her honeymoon. Her plans include going to Disney and Universal, attending a sumo event, visiting Fuji and Hiroshima, and hiring go-karts to drive around Tokyo."Of course I want to experience an authentic side of Japan but I'm excited to embrace the tourist side too and go along with it," she says.More on this story

articles.title: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sister
articles.summary: A French couple - both conceived by sperm donors - wanted children. But with home DNA tests illegal, how could they be sure they were not related?
articles.body: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sisterImage source, Courtesy of Audrey and Arthur KermalvezenImage caption, Audrey and Arthur Kermalvezen met at a gathering of donor-conceived activistsFor years, Arthur Kermalvezen, the child of a sperm donor, saw possible fathers everywhere he went. "I imagined it might be my teacher, the people I saw on the bus... and I was very angry because it's impossible to live like this."When, as an adult, he fell in love with Audrey, another sperm donor baby from Paris, the question became even more pressing.Audrey describes the moment they met at a gathering for donor conceived activists in 2010 as "love at first sight" - but was this connection a romantic or genetic attraction? When they were born, there were only two sperm banks in Paris and many men had made multiple donations - so there was a real possibility they could be half-siblings.Before building a life together, Arthur and Audrey needed to know whether they were related. But in France, laws governing genetic testing and donor anonymity made finding the answer extremely difficult.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, It is a criminal offence to take a home DNA test in FranceIn France, only a research scientist, doctor or judge can order and supervise a genetic test, and people can be fined more than €3,500 ($4,288; £3,191) for possessing a home testing kit. As a result, companies such as 23andMe, Ancestry and MyHeritage don't make their kits available in France.Supporters of the law, in place since 1994, say it stops sensitive genetic data being given to commercial companies, and prevents family disputes being caused by unexpected results.But Arthur points out that France is the only country in Europe that criminalises the use of such tests.Even before her parents told her as an adult that she was donor-conceived, Audrey had qualified as a lawyer, specialising in bioethics law. Because of this, she fully understood that French law had guaranteed donor anonymity, even after a donor's death. But Audrey had been conceived in 1979, before any such legislation existed.Image source, Courtesy of Audrey and Arthur KermalvezenImage caption, Audrey and Arthur have both campaigned for the right to know one's originsWhile searching for other donor-conceived people born before 1994, Audrey came across Arthur. He had written a book detailing his desire to learn more about his biological origins.Audrey says she was struck by how precisely he expressed feelings she herself had struggled to articulate. Both had loving families, yet both found themselves drawn to questions about the unknown people who had helped to create them.When they met in person the chemistry was immediate. So was the problem.Before they could move from platonic friendship to a romantic relationship, and even build a life together, they had to know the truth about their fathers. But no one in authority was willing to tell them.In search of the truthAfter months of searching, they found a doctor in southern France who, for €900 ($1,028; £764) in cash, conducted a genetic test which found that they were not related. But their unease remained as the doctor was breaking the law in sharing that result with them. "We were worried he was a charlatan," Audrey says.They considered using a home-testing kit to confirm the result, but as a lawyer, Audrey was determined to act within the law. So, from 2010, she launched a series of legal challenges to the French system.She wanted to know whether her donor was still alive and, if so, whether he still wished to remain anonymous. Could she access non-identifying information about how many times he had donated and whether Arthur could be among her half-siblings?Her efforts failed. After three years of legal challenges, the couple took a 'leap of faith' and got married.In 2015, France's highest administrative court rejected Audrey's final appeal. Image source, Courtesy of Audrey KermalvezenImage caption, In 2013, they took a leap of faith and got marriedShortly before the birth of their first child, a doctor agreed to investigate what information might exist about their respective donors. Under French law, a medical practitioner has access to this information about their patients, but is not allowed to share it with them. The doctor found that their donors were born in different years - and so could not be the same man. A life-changing piece of information, but one they only gained because a doctor agreed to break the rules. "It's completely weird," Audrey says, "because it means that the doctor can know more than me... about me."Even with this new information, Arthur still worried they could be related, so after years of resisting it, they finally took a home DNA test.Campaigners say the French ban has done little to stop people taking home tests, with the advocacy group DNA Pass estimating that well over a million French people have taken one. Many order them via friends in countries where they are legally obtainable - or by using forwarding services in neighbouring countries. The test said they weren't related.DNA shock The DNA results soon opened more doors. After 30 years of imagining who his father might be, Arthur finally made contact with his sperm donor on Christmas Day in 2017. But Audrey had the greatest shock. Among her DNA matches was a woman named Sophie whom she'd represented in court. The two women had been fighting for similar legal rights."I discovered that Sophie - a woman whose case I had pleaded in court - was my biological sister," Audrey says.Image source, Courtesy of Audrey KermalvezenImage caption, Arthur and Audrey finally built their familyAudrey and Arthur had taken their DNA test alongside eight other donor-conceived activists campaigning for access to their origins. Of the 10, four turned out to share the same donor: Audrey, her brother Peter, Sophie and Sophie's brother David - highlighting how real the risk of a shared donor had always been. Image source, Courtesy of Audrey and ArthurImage caption, Today, Audrey and Arthur have three children togetherMany years later, a genetic match with an American led Audrey to her donor - a man called Philippe - but he had already died.Audrey's mother wrote Philippe's family a letter, thanking them for his "gift" which she described as "immeasurable".  His family welcomed Audrey for a visit. "Everybody had tears in their eyes," recalls Audrey. Philippe's sister had never known he was a donor.The discovery gave Audrey answers that she had sought for decades. She learned details about her biological family's medical history. She saw photographs and video footage of Philippe. "I can watch him, see how he moved and hear his voice."Audrey's legal campaign and Arthur's book together helped drive changes to French donor-conception laws, allowing people conceived after April 2025 to access identifying information about their donors when they reach adulthood.For now, however, France remains one of the few countries in Europe where at-home DNA testing is still prohibited.Which means, for Audrey, the wider fight continues. "Every person has the right to know their origins and the right to know their history," she says. Based on an episode of The Gift on BBC Radio 4More weekend picks

articles.title: I've been to Gamescom six times - here's what excited me this year
articles.summary: The BBC's Laura Cress gets a first look at the biggest games in Cologne from Witcher 3 to Alien: Isolation 2.
articles.body: I've been to Gamescom six times - here's what excited me this yearFigure caption, Watch: BBC's Laura Cress on the floor at Gamescom in CologneByLaura CressTechnology reporterGamescom is the largest in-person gaming event in the world, and this year it lived up to expectations with big games on show from The Witcher 3's new expansion, to Alien: Isolation 2.Last year over 350,000 people flocked to the halls of the Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany to get a chance to see and play the most hotly anticipated games.This year that number of attendees is expected to have been even bigger, with the likes of Xbox and Sega showcasing games to the public alongside indie studios with only one or two developers.This was my sixth time attending Gamescom, which never fails to make me excited about the games industry. Here are a few of the big things I got to check out this week.The Witcher 3: Songs of the PastImage source, CD Projekt Red/Fool's TheoryImage caption, Gamers will once again play as the gruff-voiced Geralt of Rivia in the new The Witcher 3 expansionWhen CD Projekt Red announced it was making a new expansion for the hugely popular action-role playing game The Witcher 3, it came as a shock.The original, after all, came out 11 years ago.Yet it was clear sitting in the crowd for Opening Night Live on Tuesday that there's still a lot of love for the older game. There were gasps and audible shouts of joy when the team announced they were providing a free upgrade to the original.As for the expansion, Songs of the Past will follow the gruff-voiced protagonist Geralt in an adventure discovering more about the past of his close friend Dandelion.Doug Cockle, who voices Geralt, told me it was a "thrill" to return as The Witcher."I love this character so much...it's like slipping into a warm bath, or putting on an old pair of shoes," he said.Image caption, Doug Cockle, who plays Geralt, out of his Witcher uniform, alongside Laura CressFrom what I got to see, it's clear choice will once again be front and centre of the player's experience, with lots of options to choose from in how to react to people.For those hoping to take their time tossing a coin to their Witcher, the head of co-developer Fool's Theory Jakub Rokosz told me this expansion would be "on par with the size" of previous additions such as Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone.Alien: Isolation 2Alien: Isolation 2 is the long-awaited sequel to Horsham-based Creative Assembly's 2014 survival-horror game.One of the things that made the original Alien: Isolation so terrifying was its seemingly intelligent Xenomorph, which appeared to learn from your behaviour and adapt to it.Considering I physically jumped out of my seat at one point playing the demo when avoiding the Alien, it's safe to say Creative Assembly will once again be ratcheting up the tension with the sequel.This time rather than playing as the daughter of Ellen Ripley, you play as Blake, a chief executive of the infamous Weyland-Yutani corporation. Image source, Creative Assembly/SegaImage caption, The Alien is as horrifying as everAs well as claustrophobic spaceship corridors, in the sequel you will also be avoiding the Alien in bigger, open air spaces. But the game's Project Art Director Anastasia Sopikova said that did not mean you would always feel safer."You step outside. And you're like, 'Oh yeah, I'm relieved, I'm outside," she said."And then the rain picks up and it gets foggier, and you hear something nearby and you're like, 'Oh, okay.' Suddenly you realise you're really vulnerable. You're really exposed."FableRalph Fulton, the founder of Leamington Spa-based Playground Games, told me the 2027 reboot of the role-playing classic Fable had "two tonal pillars" - "Britishness" and "fairy tales".Fulton said the team was keen to avoid the generic English accents often heard in fantasy games, pointing out that "accent is such an identifier in the UK, where accents change every 15 to 20 miles".Instead, Fable features voices from across the UK, and a voice cast of over 100 actors."I want to hear people from Newcastle, from Edinburgh, from Cardiff, you know? And we've done that and it brings this incredible sense of Britishness, and also this incredible sense of humour," he said.The game is deliberately not a continuation of the original trilogy's timeline, but it will have some of its quirks, taking players into a new open-world version of Albion - the game's fairy-tale version of medieval Britain.Tomb Raider: Legacy of AtlantisLara Croft has been exploring ancient ruins and culling the local wildlife for nearly 30 years now (the original Tomb Raider came out in 1996). Legacy of Atlantis revisits Lara's original adventure, including her journey through Peru.It's not the first time the classic game has been remade, but Jeff Adams, experience director at co-developers Crystal Dynamics, told me reimagining it was still a "very delicate formula"."You have to be very intentful with where you make modifications, but you do so in the attempt to kind of bring it into a modern gameplay space." As for why after 30 years people still want to play as the twin-pistoled adventurer, Michał Kuk, Creative Director at Flying Wild Hog, said it was not just about her athletic ability."It's also about the attitude, the energy, the self-confidence," he added.Image caption, They went all out with the Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis booth this yearElsewhere at the expo, over three days some got to take part in an event called Games Done Quick (GDQ), where people try to finish a game as quickly as possible.Its previous events are often watched by hundreds of thousands of people online, with GDQ's charity marathons having raised "62 million dollars for charities in the last 16 years", according to business director Ashley Farkas. "Anybody can be a part of this community, anybody can be a speedrunner, and it is just like a giant hug from gamers of like, hey, we want you to come, hang out and do fun stuff and raise money for charity," she said.Silent Hill TownfallSilent Hill, the psychological survival horror franchise from Japanese studio Konami, has for the most part been set in America, although the most recent excursion - Silent Hill f - was based in Japan in the 1960s era. Now in Silent Hill Townfall, made by the Glasgow-based team Screen Burn, that location is in an entirely new place - Scotland, albeit a fictional part of it - St Amelia.Image caption, Silent Hill's director says the game's setting is very ScottishScotland was initially going to be more of an influence than a setting, but the team ultimately decided to embrace it fully. Director Jon McKellan told me that approach felt "more natural and kind of authentic", with the game filled with recognisably Scottish shops and signage. "It's very, very Scottish," he said.

articles.title: Cameron beats Mayer to become unified light-middleweight champion
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron produced one of the finest displays of her career to beat Mikaela Mayer and add the WBA and WBC light-middleweight titles to her WBO belt.
articles.body: This was one of Cameron's best displays. These fighters were evenly matched in every metric – from punch rate to height and weight, even hairstyle.But Cameron won out thanks to her unrelenting pressure, which never allowed the usually adaptable Mayer to figure out a winning gameplan.Mayer was the more imposing figure early on, but Cameron played counterpuncher until she could get onto the front foot.Cameron forced Mayer against the ropes in round four, and again at the start of the fifth. Increasingly confident to take the initiative, she was roared on by a partisan but disappointingly small home crowd.Mayer was unable to get in behind her jab for long periods and was bleeding and breathing heavily by round six.The home favourite was cut in the final rounds but pushed through and was lifted shoulder high by her team before her biggest win since beating Taylor in Dublin three years ago was announced.For three-weight world champion Mayer, this is the third defeat of her 25-fight career and costs her the WBA and WBC belts, which Cameron now puts with her WBO title.When this event was announced, it was the prime event of the August bank holiday weekend in British boxing.However, the elevation of Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgovic to a world title fight left this big-ticket event feeling rather undeservedly like a support act.That was reflected in the crowd, with scores of empty seats around the arena as the main undercard began. At a generous estimate, BP Pulse Arena was half-full when the fighters made their ring walks for the main event.Mayer and Cameron did their best to bring the big fight feeling in the build-up. Previously cordial relations boiled over on Friday as they butted heads at Friday's weigh-in at BP Pulse Arena.Cameron shoved her head into the American, who pushed back, before they exchanged insults side by side.On fight night, Mayer played up her away status by entering the ring to American Woman by Lenny Kravitz. She also wore a black durag over her trademark blonde hair, before removing it to show tight dreadlocks – the same style as Cameron.However, her moxie was eventually worn down by Cameron, with a big right to the chin in round seven the most notable of blows.This fight headlined the event marking the fifth anniversary of Most Valuable Promotions (MVP), the promoters fronted by Jake Paul who, since 2021, have moved from YouTuber fights to leading the way for women's boxing in the UK.Paul, influencer and co-founder of MVP, was in the house. He headlined on 29 August 2021, beating MMA fighter Tyron Woodley, but was in a watching brief here.MVP's next women's boxing arena event will take place in November in Texas.It will be headlined by unified super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner, with the American stepping up to lightweight to face IBF champion Elif Nur Turhan – on her way to a potential 2027 showdown with WBC and WBO champion Caroline Dubois.World championship fights on the undercard will include featherweight champion Tiara Brown defending against former super-bantamweight undisputed champion Ellie Scotney, and super-bantamweight champion Skye Nicolson against three-time, two-division champion Miyo Yoshida.The next fight is particularly important for Cameron, after her first bout at BP Pulse Arena since November 2024 – and first since her much-lauded move to MVP.MVP have plenty of options they could introduce from their stable. IBF light-middleweight champion Oshae Jones seems the logical next step; or IBF, WBO and The Ring middleweight belt holder Tammara Thibeault of Canada.Cameron regularly laments that she has not had the chances her talent deserves since her blockbuster double header against Taylor in 2023.Three years on, she will want fights of that level – especially after Saturday night's result.

articles.title: GB's Fery beaten in his first ATP Tour final
articles.summary: Arthur Fery misses out on his first ATP Tour title with a straight-set defeat by Ignacio Buse in the final of the Winston-Salem Open.
articles.body: Arthur Fery missed out on his first ATP Tour title with a straight-set defeat by Ignacio Buse in the final of the Winston-Salem Open.Fery, who was the talk of Wimbledon as he reached the semi-finals of his home major in July, lost 6-3 6-2 to Peru's Buse.The 24-year-old was the first Briton to reach the final of the ATP 250 tournament in North Carolina and will rise to 33 in the world rankings as a result - overtaking Cameron Norrie as British number one. Only eight weeks ago, before his astonishing run to the last four at the All England Club, he was ranked outside the top 100.Little could separate Fery and Buse in the early stages of their match on Saturday, before the Peruvian took control with a break to love for a 5-3 lead.Fery quickly fell further behind in the second set as Buse opened up a double break cushion with no reply, and while he pulled back one of those breaks, it proved to no avail as his opponent reeled off three straight games to seal the win.For 22-year-old Buse, victory makes him the youngest ever winner of Winston-Salem and marks a second career title after he beat American Tommy Paul at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg in May.With little time to reflect on his Winston-Salem run, Fery will now head to New York for the US Open, which starts on Sunday.Set to play at Flushing Meadows for the first time, he faces a tough opening tie against Italian 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.Fery is one of nine British players set to feature in the main draws at the US Open, the final Grand Slam of the season.Joining him in the men's draw are Norrie and Jan Choinski, qualifiers Toby Samuel and Harry Wendelken, and lucky loser Jacob Fearnley.Katie Boulter is joined by qualifiers Fran Jones and Harriet Dart in the women's draw, but both Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu are missing through injury.

articles.title: £300m spent, bottom of the table... but Spurs boss De Zerbi 'not angry'
articles.summary: Having spent more than £300m in the summer, Tottenham find themselves bottom of the Premier League, without a point or a goal, but boss Roberto de Zerbi remains optimistic.
articles.body: £300m spent, bottom of the table... but Spurs boss De Zerbi 'not angry'Figure caption, Jaissle claims first Premier League win at lacklustre SpursByMichael EmonsBBC Sport journalistTottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi said he was "not angry" and there was "no panic" after his side's second loss in two games left them bottom of the Premier League – but it was a depressingly familiar story for the club's fans.Goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa in a 10-minute second-half spell gave Newcastle a 2-0 victory, with thousands of Spurs supporters heading for the exits early.They have every reason to be annoyed as they have now seen only three home league wins from their past 23 matches at their superb stadium.Seventeenth in the Premier League in 2024-25, 17th in 2025-26, only avoiding relegation on the final day, but this season was meant to be different.With more than £300m spent in the summer, Spurs fans were expecting a push to get back into Europe, having won the Europa League two seasons ago and been in the last 16 of the Champions League in March.Instead, in the Premier League it is played two, lost two, scored none, 20th out of 20."We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result," said De Zerbi."Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded, we played better than Newcastle."We are disappointed for the result and [for] our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team, we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham."'I know where we are going and what the plan is'Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Roberto de Zerbi has won four, drawn two and lost four of his 10 Tottenham matches in charge in all competitionsAfter beating Everton on the final day of last season to stay up, Tottenham tried to ensure they were not in a relegation scrap this year.In came midfielders Mateus Fernandes from West Ham and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £85m and £100m respectively, defender Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52m and Manchester City winger Savio, formerly known as Savinho, for £75m, although he missed Saturday's match because of "muscle fatigue".Defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, plus goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, have arrived on free transfers and striker Omar Marmoush made his debut against Newcastle following his loan from Manchester City, with the deal becoming a permanent £60m transfer next summer.After a 3-0 loss at Brentford last week, more home pain was inflicted on the Spurs support, although the Magpies scored with both of their attempts on target as Tottenham failed to convert any of their 17 attempts, six of which were on target."Forget the result," insisted De Zerbi. "I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result."There is no panic. I know where we are going and what the plan is. I'm sorry for the fans for the result. We have to improve. We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection between the players."Old questions return early in seasonFormer Tottenham and England goalkeeper Joe Hart was not as positive about Spurs' performances and said: "The frustration in the stadium, and among the fans, will be they are looking at that Spurs team and wondering what they are trying to achieve."When you see a Newcastle side who have been through massive change over the summer - and a more difficult change than Spurs have - it's hard as in two games you can clearly see what [Newcastle boss] Matthias Jaissle is trying to do. The players are on board with it and they are flying."The concern for Tottenham is they can't say the same. But there's been a lot of change and it's not easy to bed in that many players under so much pressure."Hardly anyone has been able to find the remedy at the club so it's not like it's an easy fix. They've not just suddenly fallen off a cliff, they've been struggling in the league for a while."Roberto de Zerbi needs to get his new players to settle in quickly as the Premier League comes at you so fast, and it feels like his team are second-guessing everything at the moment."Former England goalkeeper Rob Green, speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, added: "Lukas Hornicek made some saves in the first half but Tottenham were short of invention, creation, goals."For Tottenham, the same questions last season are still here this season. Performances like this will indicate that they need a vast improvement from this set of players that have come into this club."They will need the characters as much as anything to turn this around. It doesn't take much for these Spurs fans to turn and the belief start to drain from the players."One more signing to come?Figure caption, Spurs didn't deserve defeat by Newcastle - De ZerbiThe transfer window closes on Tuesday, and on Friday De Zerbi said he was still seeking "one player more in one specific position".After the Newcastle match he was asked about the potential departures of Kevin Danso, Pape Matar Sarr and Richarlison, who have all been linked with moves away from Tottenham."I have very good relationships but if they want to leave, they have to bring the solution, the economic solution, to the club, and they can go," he said.De Zerbi was only appointed at the end of March, earning 11 points in seven matches to keep Spurs up, and insists it will not be a quick fix to the club's problems."We have to improve and to change two seasons like the last two is impossible in 10 days and with people in the transfer market," said the Italian."We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection with the players because last season before the end of the season we were in the Championship and we stayed up together."Now we have to keep calm and focus on improvement. We have a great squad and great players."More on this story

articles.title: Vicariously hike the Appalachian in the gorgeous A Trail Tale
articles.summary:
Inspired by Oregon Trail, but minus the dysentery. | Screenshot: Terrence O’Brien / The Verge	

I used to be an avid hiker and would try to go backpacking a few times a year. I always dreamed of thru-hiking the Appalachian Trail, but life kind of got in the way. (Turns out jobs, wives, and children aren't thrilled with the idea of you disappearing for three months.) But I've been longing to reconn
articles.body:
I used to be an avid hiker and would try to go backpacking a few times a year. I always dreamed of thru-hiking the Appalachian Trail, but life kind of got in the way. (Turns out jobs, wives, and children aren’t thrilled with the idea of you disappearing for three months.) But I’ve been longing to reconnect with my love of the outdoors and just recently took my kids on their first camping trip. So I discovered A Trail Tale at a really opportune time. It’s an interactive trail journal created by Andy Moliski with help from his brothers Adam and Alex.
The various segments of the trail are rendered in beautiful pixel art reminiscent of a ’90s Sierra point-and-click adventure. Alex recorded an equally gorgeous original score that combines nature sounds, acoustic guitar, strings, and even what sounds like clarinet.
As you click through each day, you’re greeted with information about landmarks and a game-like UI that is partially inspired by titles like Oregon Trail. (Spoiler: nobody dies of dysentery in this one.) Clicking on Andy unfurls a menu of icons that offer details about the journey, his mental state, and even bits of poetry. There are even little icons for things that impact his fortitude and morale meters, like inclement weather or picturesque scenery.
It’s insanely easy to just get lost in Andy’s journey for hours. And it’s making me wonder if I should get back out there and start tackling some more of the AT myself.
articles.author: Terrence O’Brien

articles.title: Man City open talks with Liverpool over Gakpo
articles.summary: The Netherlands forward has also attracted interest from Tottenham, but sources indicate Manchester City is his preferred destination if he leaves Anfield.
articles.body: Liverpool view Gakpo as a proven multi-functional Premier League attacker and he has shown that with a goal and an assist in their first two games this season.But all summer, the understanding has been that if the club bring in the attacking players they want, they would not stand in the way of Gakpo if a solid offer came in. Given how late in the transfer window the talks are taking place between Liverpool and Manchester City, the Anfield side will now consider the situation before sanctioning any move. Liverpool are also hoping to bring in another winger before deadline day.With the arrival of Victor Munoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and Barcola's imminent move from PSG, Gakpo is well aware that he may not be first choice any more, so if a move does happen it would not come as a surprise.Financially it will be a great outcome for Liverpool if they agree a deal for about £85m given they signed Gakpo for £35m from PSV Eindhoven after the World Cup in 2022.But with Hugo Ekitike missing until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles tendon, and Isak's injury struggles, they would be taking a massive risk letting Gakpo leave.

articles.title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
articles.summary: An investigation has begun into the storage of weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area.
articles.body: Thirty-seven people have died and almost 400 have been evacuated after a Russian drone strike hit a depot storing weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area on the outskirts of Kyiv.The strike caused shells, mines and drones to detonate late on Friday, triggering a blast that damaged nearby properties including a care home for the elderly and disabled, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.He said the storage site "definitely shouldn't have been there" and that an investigation had been launched into "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosive right next to people".The attack is the second to hit a munitions depot near Kyiv in recent months, prompting renewed anger.Four children are among the 42 people injured in Friday night's explosion, according to regional head Tymur Tkachenko, with a rescue operation ongoing at the site, in the Bucha district, on Saturday.Russia's Ministry of Defence said in a statement that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot" in Myla, a village to the west of the Ukrainian capital, holding "components and launch boosters for FP-1/FP-2 long-range unmanned aerial vehicles".The explosion damaged about 130 homes in the village."Everything is completely damaged," local resident Liubov Pavlenko, 45, told the BBC while inspecting her home around 200m from the ammunition warehouse."There are cracks all around the entire perimeter, and cracks around the windows. Basically, the structural integrity has been compromised," she added."I'm still kind of numb. I don't know… once I come around a little tomorrow, I'll probably have an even bigger breakdown."Zelensky said the decision to store explosives in the village was "absolutely unacceptable", adding: "Criminal proceedings have been opened on charges of official negligence."The office of Ukraine's prosecutor general earlier said it was reviewing the "legality of the placement and storage of explosive objects and materials" near residential buildings in Myla.It said the "actions of officials who made the relevant decisions" would also be investigated.However, Zelensky earlier stated that "there are regulations in place - ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas", adding "appropriate conclusions will certainly be drawn". He referenced the strike on an ammunition warehouse in Vyshneve in July, which caused a secondary detonation that killed nine, injured dozens more and damaged more than 280 homes.Friday night's explosion has raised fresh questions about why munitions were being stored so close to people's homes, especially given the regularity of Russian aerial attacks."The authorities, the Ministry of Defence - why was this allowed at the depots, in a place where there used to be food?" Borys Daniyluk, 61, said."Why were ammunition and weapons stored there, next to a populated village? There are no words, just emotions."Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky expressed regret that a "lesson" had not been learned following the explosion in Vyshneve.The investigation into that incident revealed serious failings on the part of a state-owned company that had not complied with regulations regarding storage of explosives near residential buildings.Zelensky indicated that the Myla depot had been operated by Ukraine's armed forces."In the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes over and over is criminal negligence," Koretsky said on Telegram."Everyone responsible, without exception, must face severe punishment so that such situations never happen again."Meanwhile, Tkachenko said a 14-year-old was killed in a separate attack in the Boryspil district, while Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a two-year-old had died after a Russian drone crashed in Obolonskyi.He added that five people, including an 18-year-old girl, were injured in fresh strikes on the capital on Saturday morning. Five people have been killed across the country over the past day, according to local officials.Zelensky reported further overnight strikes in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia, as the Ukrainian army said it had shot down 233 Russian drones.Russia and Ukraine have been intensifying their aerial attacks in recent months, with Kyiv focusing its operations on Russian economic targets.Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies.

articles.body:
Alt-right troll Milo Yiannopoulos was arrested by ICE on Thursday, and today the Department of Homeland Security confirmed to Reuters and The Washington Post that he had been deported to the UK. Yiannopoulos came to the US legally in 2019, but overstayed his visa. After he failed to appear in court for an immigration hearing, a final order of removal was issued ​on July 22.
The British national made a name for himself as an editor at Steve Bannon’s Breitbart and an early supporter of Donald Trump’s. He has had a long history of controversial statements and associations, including reportedly helping arrange Trump’s dinner with Kanye West and white nationalist Nick Fuentes, and he was a key figure in the online harassment campaign Gamergate.
In recent years, however, his antics have led to a falling out with most significant figures on the right, including MAGA influencer Laura Loomer. He has denied condoning statutory rape or pedophilia, but he has suggested it’s acceptable for an adult to have a sexual relationship with a 13-year-old.
There’s no word if the 44 interns in a trenchcoat who also constitute the entity known as Milo Yiannopoulos have also been deported.
articles.author: Terrence O’Brien

articles.title: Normandy veteran who lied about age to enlist dies at 101
articles.summary: A veterans' charity says Donald Turrell will be remembered with "enormous affection and gratitude".
articles.body: The charity's vice president, Dick Goodwin, said: "Don was incredibly special."He had a warmth and presence that lit up every room he entered, and he touched the lives of so many people."As a World War Two veteran, Don represented a generation whose courage and service we will never forget. "It was a privilege for the taxi charity to know him, and he will be remembered with enormous affection and gratitude. "My thoughts are with his family and all those who loved him at this very sad time."In an interview last year, Turrell said: "I did lie about my age. I pushed it up a bit, gave all the right answers, and I was in. I was happy."He explained he had always wanted to be a soldier and that like "all the young lads" he had wanted to play his part in defending his country.The veteran described feeling "excited and apprehensive" during the crossing to the Normandy coast, and said his "introduction" to the war was seeing bodies from earlier fighting washing back up on the beach as he landed.His war came to an end a few weeks later on July 10, when he was seriously injured during fighting near the town of Eterville. He was later medically discharged.Turrell spoke movingly of the close friends he lost during the campaign, some of whom he buried in the field, and who are now buried in Commonwealth war cemeteries on the continent. The war also claimed his older brother Leslie, who had been a telegraphist on HMS Penelope and died when she was sunk off the Italian coast near Naples in February 1944.Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.

articles.title: Hy4 preview
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://www.tencent.com/tencent-releases-and-open-sources-tencent-hy4-preview/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49492632
Points: 357
# Comments: 215
articles.body:
Ranked among the top tier of open-source models, Hy4 preview is built for real-world productivity tasks, delivering outstanding performance across coding, office work, and scientific research
Tencent has released and open-sourced Tencent Hy4 preview, a next-generation large language model with 770B total parameters and 49B active parameters, and a context window exceeding 1M tokens. It demonstrates outstanding capabilities on real-world productivity tasks spanning coding, office work, and scientific research.
Hy4 preview is now available as an open-source model and can also be accessed globally through WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy, as well as Yuanbao, ima and other Tencent products. Users can try the model directly through these applications, or connect to it via API through Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter.
Upon launch, Hy4 preview will be available for free on WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy for two weeks. Free access to Hy3 on both platforms has also been extended until September 30.
Hy4 preview was expanded significantly in model size, context length, and data volume, and  the advances in both pre-training and post-training have led to a major leap in overall intelligence, placing the model among the top tier of open-source models.
Hunyuan continuously works in deep co-design with products such as CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy, optimizing the real-world user experience across productivity scenarios. In a blind evaluation conducted internally by Tencent involving 163 experts and 203 engineering tasks, Hy4 preview scored an average of 2.99 out of 4.00, slightly ahead of GLM-5.3 (2.92/4.00) and Kimi K3 (2.94/4.00).
Designed for productivity, Hy4 preview was developed using high-quality training data co-created with Tencent experts across software engineering, gaming, finance, security, and other domains, as well as through deep co-design with products such as WorkBuddy. This has helped drive significant improvements across a wide range of real-world productivity tasks.
In software engineering, Hy4 preview delivers stronger understanding, planning, debugging, and validation capabilities for long-context development tasks, while also enhancing the visual quality and interaction experience of front-end development.
In office productivity and analytical scenarios, the model demonstrates a significantly stronger understanding of complex working environments and enhanced financial analysis capabilities. It has also been optimized for data analysis and cross-document collaboration, supporting the full workflow from information processing through to the creation of documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
In game development, Hy4 preview can generate a playable prototype from a single natural-language request, and work effectively with game engines. Developers can then continue refining complex game projects through multi-turn interactions.
In scientific research, Hy4 preview demonstrates stronger capabilities in understanding, reasoning through and solving complex research problems, with notable improvements across areas including AI research and development, molecular dynamics simulation, condensed-matter physics and fundamental mathematics.
Notably, Hy4 preview also contributed to its own development process, participating for the first time in the automated optimization of training methods, data strategies, evaluation frameworks, and low-level operators. The model proposed approaches, ran experiments, and iterated based on the results, with the resulting code, logs, and feedback feeding into subsequent rounds of exploration. This established an early-stage recursive self-improvement loop.
Hy4 preview has also autonomously analyzed bottlenecks in its inference system  and carried out multiple rounds of optimization on areas such as operator fusion and communication optimization. These improvements increased end-to-end throughput by 31.8% compared with the baseline, with consistent gains across different context lengths and concurrency levels. This demonstrates the model’s ability to autonomously optimize its own inference infrastructure.
Hy4 preview continues to offer cost efficiency, helping make advanced AI more widely accessible. API pricing is set at USD 0.834 per million input tokens, USD 2.501 per million output tokens and USD 0.042 per million tokens for cache hits.
Through a preview-first approach, followed by official releases, Hunyuan continuously incorporates real-world feedback into its research and development process, enabling its models to improve by solving real-world problems. The next batch of models in the Hy4 series is expected to roll out soon.

articles.title: Decision to curtail play at Lord's 'a joke' - Hussain
articles.summary: The decision to abandon play an hour early after a rain-hit third day of England’s second Test against Pakistan is criticised by former captain Nasser Hussain and fans.
articles.body: The decision to abandon play an hour before scheduled at the end of the third day of England's second Test against Pakistan was called "a joke" by Nasser Hussain.On a Saturday badly affected by persistent showers at Lord's, players left the field at 17:08 BST.At that point, prospects of conditions improving sufficiently for play to resume seemed remote. However, rain cleared and the sky brightened.The groundstaff partially removed the covers while officials deliberated. At 18:30, with up to an hour of playing time remaining and with the weather the best it had been all day, umpires Paul Reiffel and Allahuddien Parker abandoned proceedings.The decision was greeted with booing by some of the sparse crowd that remained inside the ground."That's a joke, honestly a joke," former England captain Hussain said on Sky Sports."I earlier said how good the umpires have been. These fans have waited all afternoon for it to stop raining. It's now bright. There's blue sky in the distance. That is an unbelievable decision, it really is."In about five minutes' time it's going to be sunny here."The weather stayed dry and the light remained good up to 19:30, the time at which play would have been scheduled to close.The morning session had been washed out and only 24.5 overs of play were possible as the players dodged the showers, meaning spectators will receive a 50% refund on the price of their ticket.If 30 overs had been completed, spectators would not have been entitled to any money back.Still, the abandonment caused some fans to express their displeasure with messages to the BBC's live coverage of the Test."Sat in the Edrich Stand," wrote Joe at Lord's. "It hasn't rained for half an hour and it's as bright as it's been all day. Absolutely no justification for not playing right now. A real shame."Rachel in Kingswinford added: "Ridiculous to call it off! They want fans supporting Test cricket and those spectators have stuck with it all day - another 30-45 mins of play would have been a better look (plus saving authorities money on refunds)!"Another message from Paul in Northwich read: "This is a terrible advert for cricket. It's like the umpires are waiting for it to rain again. At least the spectators can get a refund."Play ended with England 177-7 in their second innings, 357 ahead and on course to win the match and series.Batting conditions had been difficult all day and it would have been another challenging period for the home side had they been asked to return for a short time late in the evening."It would have been a tricky 40 minutes to go out there and bat," said Dan Lawrence, who made an unbeaten 50."It's nice to have a good sleep and think about how I'm going to play in the morning. I can imagine it will be with the same intent and trying to push the game forward."Forty minutes of batting at 6.45pm is never an ideal thing."The situation at Lord's came on the same day Durham were denied the chance to chase a victory target of four against Gloucestershire because of bad light at the end of the third day of their County Championship match at Chester-le-Street.It means the teams will return on Sunday for what could be as little as one ball of action.Gloucestershire were dismissed for 250 in their second innings in the closing stages of Saturday, with visiting coach Mark Alleyne claiming the light was already too poor before his team were all out."I'm not sure where to start, really," said Alleyne. "I mean, 45 minutes before we lost the last wicket, it was too dark to play, which would have been consistent with all the other days that we played.""We had probably 50 minutes of cricket there that we probably shouldn't have done."The match could have been concluded had Gloucestershire chosen to bowl spin, only for the away side to refuse and push the game into a Sunday when rain is forecast."They asked if we would bowl our spinners to finish the game," added Alleyne. "Of course, we said no, we'll bowl our quick bowlers, in which case it became bad light, so we'll come back tomorrow."Durham coach Ryan Campbell wrote on X: "Cricket sometimes doesn't help itself. Before everyone loads up on the poor old umpires, it's not their fault."

articles.title: Pogacar requires surgery after Vuelta crash
articles.summary: Tadej Pogacar needs surgery on a broken collarbone after sustaining multiple injuries in the crash that led to him abandoning the Vuelta a Espana.
articles.body: Tadej Pogacar requires surgery on a broken collarbone after sustaining multiple injuries in the crash that led to him abandoning the Vuelta a Espana.Race leader and world champion Pogacar, who was aiming to complete a full set of Grand Tour victories, crashed with about 33km remaining of Saturday's eighth stage and was taken to hospital.In an update on Saturday night, his team's doctor said the 27-year-old suffered a concussion, a "stable" fracture in his neck and multiple abrasions, in addition to his broken left clavicle (collarbone). "Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout," said Dr Adrian Rotunno, UAE Team Emirates' medical director."He will require clavicle surgery which will be delayed due to concussion precautions."Tadej remains under the care of our medical team and we'll provide further updates following the surgery."Pogacar was riding in the midst of the peloton when he came off his bike, having suddenly swerved to his right and colliding with another rider. He was hit from behind by multiple other riders.The Slovenian appeared to try to get back on his bike before shaking his head and sitting down again.He then walked unaided into an ambulance. It is the first time he has abandoned a Grand Tour.The overwhelming favourite to win the three-week race had started the stage three minutes 50 seconds clear of Spaniard Enric Mas in second place.In what was a chaotic race, another crash occurred in the finishing straight as France's Bryan Coquard claimed his first stage win in a Grand Tour.The 34-year-old edged Lidl-Trek rider Mads Pedersen in a photo finish."I think it has been 13 years - it has been a lot of work and I have finished second a lot of times," Coquard told TNT Sports."I have not been in good positions in the first two sprints, I know I have good legs. Maybe I climb better now, I am fast again."Movistar rider Mas now leads the general classification by one minute  11 seconds from Decathlon CMA CGM rider Felix Gall.He is the first Spaniard to lead the Vuelta since Jesus Herrada in 2018 but a sombre Mas opted not to wear the red jersey when presented with it on the podium, instead holding it in front of him."It's a real shame," Mas said about Pogacar. "I hope he gets better quickly. We've still got a few races left and I hope he'll be in good shape for them."Six-time Grand Tour winner Pogacar was on course to win all three of the sport's biggest stage races, having already won five Tours de France and a Giro d'Italia.Having become the joint most successful Tour de France champion of all time last month, the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider is aiming to become the ninth rider to win all three Grand Tours.Pogacar has also won almost all of the sport's biggest races. In addition to his multiple stage race victories, the two-time road world champion has won 13 one-day monument races, including the Tour of Flanders (three times), Milan-San Remo (once), Il Lombardia (five times) and Liege-Bastogne-Liege (four times).In 2025, he recorded his best finish of second in the other monument - Paris-Roubaix.Pogacar was going to win the Vuelta a Espana by a country mile.Many observers believed his margin of victory could be more than 10 minutes given this much-loved three-week slog typically contains a slightly lower calibre of lead rider.Pogacar was here to further cement his dominance among current riders by becoming only the ninth man to win all three Grand Tours (Tour de France, Giro d'Italia and Vuelta a Espana).He rarely comes to grief on the road; such is his deft bike handling, he never seems to have to wrestle with the handlebars or ever wobble his way down a descent.But this shocking end to Pogacar's Vuelta demonstrates that no-one is invincible.Pogacar won't be entirely devastated - there is plenty of career time for him have another stab at this race. But it is unclear at this stage whether he will be able to defend his coveted rainbow world champion's jersey, given the Road World Championships take place in Canada next month.Vuelta audiences spiked because of the presence of the world's greatest rider for a week, but now there is a real race for the red jersey. At least six previously well-beaten riders suddenly have a shot at glory.

articles.title: Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://claude.com/blog/how-warp-builds-self-improving-agents-on-claude
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49492432
Points: 30
# Comments: 20
articles.body:
In our series, , we highlight how startups are transforming their industries with AI. In this article, we share how Warp turned stateless user feedback into a self-improvement loop for its agents.
Rust, Golang, GitHub Actions, internal agent orchestration platform (Oz), Claude Platform
$73M raised. 800K monthly developers build on Warp. 56% of the Fortune 500 uses Warp. 10M Claude Code sessions run inside Warp to date, 400K+ per week. 40M total Warp Agent conversations.
Agents need to handle recurring tasks reliably and effectively. A first-pass prompt that gets 80% of the task correct can create a noisy and annoying experience for the user. Warp learned this the hard way, and used this to inform its product strategy, creating an improved experience for nearly 1M developers worldwide.Warp, the AI-powered terminal and agentic development environment, builds on the Claude Platform. The team ran into this “noisy experience” problem with their internal code review agent. Engineers complained that their agent made unhelpful comments and produced low-quality output.The team initially tried stopgap solutions, like manually rewriting the prompt based on observed code review failures. This made output more usable but didn’t scale. Improving context files like AGENTS.md also helped, but was far from a complete fix. Ultimately, they realized, the real issue was that feedback to an agent, no matter what its purpose, typically disappears when the session ends, removing critical context from the agentic loop. Their solution: an Agent Skills-based framework to create self-improving agents where feedback compounds over time to continually refine and enhance agent output. Read on to learn how they built it with skills on top of the Claude Platform. Agent self-improvement loops built on skillsThe central technique is a self-improvement loop using skills, which are file based encodings of knowledge that keep instructions out of the raw prompt. Warp evolved a self-improving agent architecture consisting of two skills, with human feedback in between. The inner/base skill holds the functional domain knowledge and instructions. For example, when a PR is opened, Warp’s code agent executes using that base skill and context to produce its review.Human feedback on agent output is a critical component for the self-improvement loop. For code review this could be something as simple as a thumbs up, but the more explicit the better.  “A human could affirm, ‘this was a good, useful comment’,” Warp founder Zach Lloyd explains, “But the human could also give detailed reasons why a code review wasn't good. Specifics like ‘you suggested renaming this variable, but our code base convention is this type of global variable uses this particular naming context’ tell the agent how to do it right next time.”The outer/improver skill functions as an observer agent that runs on a schedule rather than per-task. It pulls the accumulated human feedback, compares what the agent suggested against how humans responded, and proposes a small, focused edit to the base skill.Because skills are plain files, agents are extremely good at updating them. These updates, which are reviewable, approvable, and mergeable, can flow through a normal PR/code-review workflow; once merged, the next run of the inner skill inherits the improvement. Warp now runs this pattern across its entire open-source repo, with separate spec-writing, review, and triage agents, each carrying their own self-improvement loop.“File-based skills are a way of encoding knowledge for agents without putting that knowledge directly in the prompt, as something the agent can simply look up in the course of doing its job,” says Zach. “The framework is really simple actually: there's the base domain-specific skill and then there's the improver skill that refines  that domain-specific skill. This simplicity is the beauty of this approach.”How to write self-improving skills for agentsHere are some of the Warp team’s tried and true tips for writing self-improving skills for agentic loops: Write principles, not rules. "Construct the skill as though you're instructing a smart person, not like you're programming a computer,” Zach says. “Including direction in the skill like ’Look for repeated code’ provides better direction than exhaustive variable naming rules.” Explain the why. Providing the rationale behind the rule lets the agent reason about the problem instead of following rigid instructions, again allowing for better generalization. Make feedback effortless to give. Capture it where people already work, like by commenting directly on a PR or issue. Also, make this happen automatically, with no extra submission step. “Low friction is what keeps signal flowing,” Zach notes. “If you make it too hard you're not going to get the feedback and you're not going to be able to improve the skill."Keep skills small and use progressive disclosure. A good skill file isn't large; it references resource files and scripts rather than dumping everything into context at once. Feedback quality > volume, but volume helps. A small amount of detailed, domain-specific feedback from a senior engineer can be worth more than lots of cursory feedback because binary thumbs up/down doesn't say why. “You can get really good signal even from a relatively small sample size if it's very detailed feedback from a person around domain specific knowledge that the agent otherwise would have no way of getting,” Zach continues. “That said, the bigger the corpus of quality signal, the better. At Warp we're using a loop to manage our whole open source repo. We have hundreds of people contributing and we're doing thousands of code reviews.”Put extra effort into the improver skill. Putting extra effort into writing the improver skill (the observer agent) pays off beyond the immediate agent loop, because improver skills are very reusable across different use cases.  “Outside of the domain specific knowledge component, this is a fairly reusable mechanism—the improver skill for a code review agent is not that different from the improver skill for any other agent.”The loop in action: Warp’s issue triage agent Warp’s issue triage agent demonstrates the self-improving agent skills framework. The pattern is triggered whenever someone files a new GitHub issue: a GitHub Action fires an agent that analyzes the issue for complexity and feasibility, assigns labels, and suggests a direction for the fix. That triage agent runs off an inner skill file holding the domain knowledge about what each label means and how to research the codebase before acting.On a sample issue, the first-stage inner skill did a solid job but missed one label, ready to spec, which signals that a contributor can start building product and technical specs against the issue. A maintainer on the Warp team caught the gap and left feedback directly on the issue, exactly where the work was happening. Critically, he explained both what he expected and why he expected it: actionable feedback easy for the agent to absorb later. The outer improver skill runs in Oz, Warp's agent orchestration platform, as a scheduled “update triage” agent. The agent authenticated to GitHub, ran a Python script bundled with the skill to pull recent issues carrying feedback, summarized them into a JSON file, and read that back into context. The bundled script is itself a best practice; skills can reference resource files instead of writing fresh code on every run.From there, the agent identified the concrete feedback signals in the maintainer comments and proposed the smallest edit that captured them. It opened a PR editing the inner skill to apply the "ready to spec" label when an issue describes a real problem, even though the exact UI or UX shape is not yet defined. Because the whole update is a skill file, it moves through the normal code-review workflow. The PR arrived with a description explaining which signals prompted the change and what it altered. A human reviews, approves, and merges, and the next run of the triage skill inherits the new knowledge. That final human step closes the loop and keeps a person in control of what actually changes.This is the same mechanism Warp now runs at scale across its open-source repo, where spec-writing agents, review agents, and triage agents each carry their own self-improvement loop. Any agent, no matter what its task, gets better over time if you build one of these loops into it from the start to capture human feedback signals, turn them into skill updates, and expand agents from one-off helpers into capable systems that compound across your org.
Best practices from the Warp team
Are you conflating skills with memory?
Skills are procedural and stable—"how to do X," run-agnostic, changed deliberately. Memory is auto-written by the agent at inference time and never stops changing.
Do you need one improver loop, or one per agent?
Meet in the middle: a templated base loop captures the overlap across your agents, with domain-specific weights layered on. A handful of improvers can each own one; a hundred should share.
What happens when the feedback is wrong?
Assume it will be. Don't let the agent accept feedback blindly — give it context to sanity-check, filter whose input counts, and keep a human in the loop at either the filtering or final-review stage.
Build the verification harness first, then let the agent tune against it: generate a reference corpus, compare output to reference, fix, repeat.
And if it isn't domain verifiable?
Lean on deterministic evals against golden outputs wherever they exist. Where you must use human feedback, restrict it to domain experts — don't open the floodgates.
How do you know the whole system is improving?
Track the global metrics humans already eyeball—time to merge, contributor count, cost—and feed them back into the improver agents. Go crawl-walk-run on deployment.
View the full webinar for a live demo and deeper discussion of how Warp uses Claude to build agents that learn from team feedback and improve themselves over time.Start building with the Claude Platform today.
