articles.body:
Africa’s Wild Dogs Are the Most Hated Carnivores on the Continent. Here’s Why Some Conservationists Are Saving Them Anyway
Meet the team that closely monitors the playful canines, which need help to form diverse packs and stop their numbers from dwindling
A pair of African wild dogs at Tswalu Kalahari Reserve, the largest privately owned nature reserve in South Africa, near the Botswana border.
Two white pickup trucks are parked beside a highway that cuts through the Waterberg, a South African municipality three hours from Johannesburg. Passing the trucks on foot, you might hear something that makes you stop: Their cargo is panting. Just visible through the holes at the top of three green wooden crates is fur over rib cages, mottled black, white and gold, rising and falling.
The three sleeping female African wild dogs, sisters, have traveled a long way in the past few weeks, even by the standards of their species, which can cover 30 miles a day and occupy ranges of 1,000 miles. They arrived by plane from Karingani Game Reserve in Mozambique, courtesy of the Endangered Wildlife Trust’s African wild dog range expansion program. The project, which started in 1997, has increased the world’s wild dog population by more than 344 in 29 years. It introduces dogs to wildlife reserves in countries where they haven’t been seen in decades—for instance, Mozambique, where the species disappeared during a civil war that lasted from 1977 to 1992. The Mozambican packs have bred so successfully that the Endangered Wildlife Trust (EWT) is now bringing young dogs to South Africa to form new, genetically diverse packs here. The three sisters have been darted with sedatives, a risky but necessary step in moving them to their new home for the next few weeks—a state-of-the-art enclosure, or boma, the first designed specifically to hold their species—before they’re released, with tracking collars, into the wild.
The sisters represent a not insignificant portion of 6,600 African wild dogs left in the world. According to the World Wildlife Fund, the animals are among the world’s most endangered. Also known as Cape hunting or painted dogs, they resemble large, gangly mongrels with extremities picked from a safari odds-and-ends bin: big, disc-shaped black ears, large paws on skinny legs and fluffy white tails. Each dog’s fur has a clearly unique pattern of black, gold and white splotches—more Abstract Impressionist than the designs that cover snakes, zebras or leopards.
Jana Pauwels, a veterinarian working with the Endangered Wildlife Trust, positions herself to tranquilize an African wild dog in an enclosure.
EWT workers Joseph Hlako and Eugene Greyling carry a sedated dog to the truck so it can be relocated, collared and then released into the wild.
Wild dogs are the most successful hunters in Africa, with a kill rate of 80 percent. Lions, by comparison, kill just 30 percent of what they hunt. The dogs’ superpower is also part of the reason they are so threatened. Owners of many private game reserves would rather kill them than lose expensive game. Subsistence farmers feel the same way about their livestock. A 2021 study published in Ecology and Evolution showed that human causes—including direct killing and diseases from domestic dogs—accounted for 44 percent of all wild dog deaths at study sites in Kenya, Botswana and Zimbabwe over a 15-year period. A lack of continuity between areas where the dogs are welcome means that without intervention, they struggle to find mates.
But there is much to love about the most hated carnivore in Africa. Ask a wild dog enthusiast what they enjoy the most, and they will likely say it is the dogs’ playfulness. Briana Abrahms, who researches wild dogs in Botswana, has seen the pups “bat around balls of elephant dung like a football.” Neil Jordan, a biologist at the University of New South Wales in Australia, discovered that wild dogs are one of the few species on Earth that appear to vote. Before departing on a hunt, the animals hold “rallies”: At dusk, one or two will stand up after resting in the heat and pull their ears back, pretending to stalk prey. They’ll make strange, strangled barks and chittering noises, curling their tongues, playing with one another and urinating.
“And then they kind of snowball socially, so then more get involved, and more get involved. It’s like a big merry-go-round, and they’re all running around crazy,” Jordan says. Typically they’ll do this once, then lie back down, then again, then lie back down. Only when they emit “rapid nasal exhalations,” or sneezes, will they actually depart. (“We still don’t know for sure whether the dogs are using that, or it just happens to be occurring around the same time as they’re signaling their intention to move in another way,” Jordan emphasizes.) Wild dogs also allow their pups to feed first, near-unique behavior among animals, says Jordan. When a member of the pack is injured or sick or heavily pregnant and can’t join a hunt, another dog will regurgitate food for it. Wild dogs look out for one another.
While the sisters doze in the trucks, I take a seat in a hut nearby with Eugene Greyling, one of the EWT field officers transporting the dogs. We’re sitting at the entrance to the Welgevonden Game Reserve, which houses the enclosure that will temporarily contain the dogs. South Africa has four main wild dog populations. The first is in captivity in private zoos. Then there is the population in Kruger National Park, which is the only place in the country with enough dogs to maintain themselves genetically. The third is the free-ranging population, roaming across a patchwork of private and public lands in the Waterberg. Finally, there is a “meta population,” whose members are tracked as they travel through nature reserves such as Welgevonden or the Tswalu Kalahari Reserve, South Africa’s largest privately owned nature reserve. EWT works with the reserves to create new, genetically diverse packs and expand their range.
Did you know? Where do wild dogs fall in their family tree?
DNA evidence suggests that African wild dogs split off from wolves, jackals and coyotes around 1.7 million years ago, making this species one of the older branches of the dog family tree.
A pack of African wild dogs can bring down prey up to 10 times its own body weight.
Trucks carry the sedated wild dogs to Welgevonden Game Reserve. Born in Mozambique, they are being relocated to a region known as the Waterberg, one of the world’s last havens for their species.
Hlako checks on one of the sedated dogs shortly after its capture. The newest EWT crates are outfitted with temperature gauges and solar-powered cameras for remote monitoring.
Hlako and Greyling release one of the dogs at Welgevonden. The reserve hosts around 65 types of mammals, including the “Big Five” safari animals: lions, leopards, African elephants, rhinoceroses and Cape buffaloes.
Wild dog packs, which consist of between 5 and 20 individuals, have complicated social structures, says Greyling. At the top is the alpha female. She and the alpha male are the only dogs in the pack who breed. In order for populations to grow, dogs must form new packs. A group of sisters will set off in one direction in search of males from another pack, while a group of brothers does the same in a different direction. The EWT carefully monitors dispersal and the packs’ genetics. The lack of continuity between ranges means the animals are likely to get stuck without a mate. Conservationists can’t afford to let sleeping dogs lie.
The three sisters in the truck, for example, had found males back in Mozambique who were too closely related. “We had to think hard about how to manage that, because technically the dogs had done everything right,” says Cole du Plessis, who coordinates the range-expansion project. “If you told people 20 years ago that we were going to be flying wild dogs under sedation to other countries—it’s just quite crazy.”
A wild dog in the new boma, or enclosure, at Welgevonden. Its large ears help it communicate in the pack, detect approaching prey and release body heat in a region where temperatures can exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit.
At Welgevonden, Greyling and I are joined in the hut by Reilly Mooney, a biologist and the director of the Waterberg Wild Dog Initiative. Mooney has traveled farther than the dogs: She came from Wisconsin to South Africa, originally to study primates. During the Covid-19 pandemic, her regular research shut down and she attended a community meeting about free-roaming dogs that had been mostly left to their own devices. “It was a very volatile situation,” Mooney says. Locals were calling for someone to bridge the gap between communities and conservationists, and Mooney was the right person for the job. The first thing on her to-do list was to find out how many dogs there were. Their coats made them relatively easy to identify and keep track of. “We can say with pretty good confidence that in this entire Waterberg area, there are only 27 wild dogs,” she says.
In the hut, Greyling gets a call from Joseph Hlako, his colleague at the EWT who has been keeping an eye on the sleeping dogs. Hlako, the EWT’s conflict mitigation officer, grew up in the area and has family who farm. He speaks Northern Sotho, among other South African languages, and has an insider’s knowledge about what will and won’t work when it comes to dogs and people. Building trust and maintaining relationships make the biggest factor, he says. “And, you know, a familiar face works better than any face.”
After Greyling leaves the hut, he drives back past us: One of the dogs seems to be overheating, he says. He wants to get her to the enclosure right away and cool her down. Mooney and I jump into her car and follow Greyling. We cross the highway, passing cattle and thick bushland until we come to the boma: a couple of shipping containers and a fence.
It doesn’t seem like much, but du Plessis designed everything in the boma specifically, and simply, for wild dogs. At the base of the fences is a concrete wall that extends four feet into the ground—wild dogs are determined diggers. The enclosure is split so that males and females can be kept apart, bonding over time through the fence. And in each section is a feeding post. The dogs tend to eat facing you, Mooney explains, which makes it hard to dart them for transportation. But if their food is tied to a post, and behind the post is a small wooden wall, the dogs are forced to eat with their behinds toward you. Conveniently, they raise their hindquarters in the air while eating, which makes for a safer and easier shot.
Hydration time at Tswalu, a luxury resort where nightly rates start at $2,800 per guest. Tswalu is deeply involved in conserving wild dogs and promotes them as a special attraction.
African wild dogs are known for youthful frolicking that extends into adulthood. The wrestling is generally playful—unlike wolves, the dogs rarely show aggression toward members of their own pack.
As we help Greyling and Hlako lift a crate off the pickup, a dusty paw flops out of one corner, and I think of something my uncle says: “You can smell the world in a dog’s paw.” Mooney and I back away, watching from inside a container as Hlako moves the car so that the overheating dog is in the shade. Though it is late afternoon, the temperature is still around 90 degrees.
Hlako and Greyling release the dogs one at a time, opening the crate and waiting until a dog walks, then trots, out. The first is less sure on her feet, the second seems almost normal, until Mooney points out that she would have run much faster from the crate and people had she not still been a bit dozy. The sisters stand together in a grassy area, point their noses in the air, move their satellite-dish ears and lie down under a thorn tree; it has been a long day.
The sun is about to set, and I need to leave before the park gates close. I prepare to say goodbye and walk over to the overheating dog, who is lying next to the water. She hasn’t stood up. She is breathing, her mouth is open, and Greyling tries to reassure everyone that she’ll be all right. But he doesn’t sound too sure.
Later, he gives me news that the dog died. It is the first time this has happened on his watch, and it comes as a shock. The cause of death is determined to be “capture myopathy,” or “broken-­heart syndrome,” says du Plessis. It is caused by heightened stress. In this case, the known factors were the stress of being captured, which involved hours of people trying to dart her, and the high temperature that day. There may have been underlying physical factors, or there may have been predators like hyenas nearby in the nights before the move. But du Plessis is focused on what the EWT could control. “I would never accept the loss of a dog as fine,” he says. But if one of the surviving sisters goes on to have puppies, and the population grows by 20 to 30 dogs in her lifetime, “then it makes it seem a little bit better.”
A year later, du Plessis updates me on the two surviving sisters. After keeping them for two months at the boma near Welgevonden, du Plessis sent them to a small private game reserve called Rietspruit, which is connected to Kruger National Park. He knew of an eligible bachelor living just nine hours away, in KwaZulu-Natal Province. Du Plessis darted the male and drove him to Rietspruit. “The bonding between those dogs went extremely well, and we had this new pack of three,” he says. “They were hunting successfully. Everything was really good. And then in October last year, that male was killed by a lion on the reserve.”
A couple more months passed, and du Plessis heard of two other males who had dispersed from a pack, looking for mates. He darted them, put them in the boma and waited for the sisters to show up. A few days later, the females, now roaming free and wearing collars, showed up near one of the reserve’s lodges. Du Plessis drove to where they were and attached two balls of hay from the boma, saturated with the males’ scent, to the back of his car. He performed “hoo-calls,” mimicking sounds the dogs make to find each other. The females emerged. Then he started to drive. “We were at one point going 60 kilometers an hour [about 37 miles per hour] while these females were keeping up, trying to get to this ball of grass,” he says. “It was one of the coolest things I’ve done in my wild dog career.”
Relocations don’t work if the dogs’ range doesn’t keep expanding and community education efforts don’t continue. But over the past three decades, the amount of land set aside for the dogs has grown by 1.5 million hectares, and there are 30 more packs than before. “The genetic diversity within those packs is very good,” du Plessis says. “If we can keep this strong and working, and other organizations are doing their restoration efforts and community conservation efforts, it’s creating the space where we’re ready to jump when the time is right.”
An overhead view of the wild dog enclosure at Welgevonden. The space features separate drinking and splash pools, an underground den and a nearby mini-clinic.
As creatures of the open savanna, African wild dogs must cover vast distances. Over the millennia, they’ve evolved longer legs and larger lungs than other wild canines.
A short way from the enclosure, du Plessis dropped the hay and sped off, trusting that the females would find their way to the males. And they did. They wasted no time flirting through the fence as wild dogs do: ducking under each other, dipping their heads. Du Plessis decided to release the males from the boma. But instead of the males coming out, the females ran in, and all four refused to emerge. So he left them to get to know one another in the enclosure for three weeks. The week du Plessis and I spoke, the females had started estrus, and the males were showing mate guarding behavior. In a few months, with any luck: puppies.
When we speak a few months later, du Plessis tells me one of the sisters did get pregnant. The pack of four made a den, something that happens only a day or so before a female gives birth. But in the next few weeks, a leopard attacked and killed the female. The puppies were too young to survive without her milk and died, too. And the remaining three went on the run again, all the way out of the park. The brothers were caught in a snare line and died, and the last surviving sister eventually joined another pack.
I ask du Plessis how he manages to not get too discouraged. “To me it’s about population trend,” he says. “Even if half of them make it, the point is the trend is growing.” In 2025, the dogs the project looks after—in South Africa, Mozambique and Malawi—had 150 puppies altogether. With only 700 breeding pairs and 6,600 wild dogs left, 150 is “quite substantial,” du Plessis says. “You have ebbs and flows, but at the end of each year, if you’re either stable or increasing, for an endangered species, you’re doing pretty well.”

articles.title: Apple TV is raising its subscription prices again
articles.summary: Now, Apple TV subscriptions will cost $14.99 per month, up from its previous price of $12.99 per month.
articles.body:
7:36 AM PDT · August 28, 2026
For the fourth time in four years, Apple TV is hiking its subscription prices.
Now, Apple TV subscriptions will cost $14.99 per month, up from the previous $12.99 per month. The annual subscription cost will also jump from $99 to $119.
Apple One, the bundle that includes subscriptions to services like iCloud+, TV, Music, and Arcade, will now cost $21.95 per month, up from $19.95.
Apple isn’t alone in hiking prices for its subscriptions. Netflix raised its prices in March, and Peacock announced a price increase earlier this month. Tech companies are also raising hardware prices, given ongoing RAM and component shortages due to massive demand for hardware for building AI data centers.
Consumers’ dismay with Apple likely won’t last long, given that the company will announce its newest slate of iPhones, which will likely include its first foldable model, on September 9.

articles.title: Verschlimmbesserung: The Word Your Software Updates Need
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://geekyschmidt.com/post/2026-08-25-verschlimmbesserung/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49479072
Points: 141
# Comments: 96
articles.body: The German language has a word for what your last software update did.It is called Verschlimmbesserung: an attempted improvement that only makes things worse.We have all lived through the SaaS update that moved a button, renamed a menu, and broke a workflow we relied on daily. Some product team shipped a “better experience” that solved a problem nobody had.Eliyahu Goldratt nailed the root cause decades ago:“Tell me how you measure me, and I will tell you how I will behave. If you measure me in an illogical way… do not complain about illogical behaviour…”When point releases become more important than the product itself, you are incentivising Verschlimmbesserung. Your engineering teams are not failing. They are optimising for the metrics you gave them.How you measure and incentivise your teams tells them exactly what you value. If the metric rewards churn, you get churn. If the metric rewards shipping, you get shipping; whether it improves anything or not.Is new always better? Probably not. Office 2003 is still incredibly useful because nobody forced it to constantly reinvent itself.Stability is a feature. Knowing when not to ship is an engineering discipline.The Germans built a word for it. Perhaps we should start using it.

articles.title: Get your Windows license refund
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://en.refund4freedom.org/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49478340
Points: 602
# Comments: 244
articles.body:
Get your Windows license refund now!
We all know the joy of acquiring a new laptop and the excitement of exploring its features and functionalities. However, the vast majority of laptops are only sold with a specific proprietary operating system: Microsoft Windows.				The vendors do not remove the Windows license, and you must pay the entire price, even if you do not want to use this system.
This is unfair and we want to change it!				Consumers should be able to buy laptops without any specific operating system, and should not have to pay the license price if they don't want to.
You should not have to pay for software you don't want. Devices like laptops and smartphones are general purpose computers so, they should be neutral in relation to the software they run. Manufacturers and vendors should not have the right to impose specific operating systems on you. When you request a refund, the process should be easy, quick and straightforward. Here’s what we demand:
Do not restrict users to specific software. Device manufacturers and vendors should not impose an operating system or software on consumers, and should not force them to pay for software that they don't want. Laptops and smartphones are general purpose computers, so consumers should be able to run the software they want on their devices.
Transparent pricing. Consumers should have the right to decline pre-installed software, including the operating system, but still be able to buy the laptop without it.
Hassle-free refunds. Manufacturers and vendors should clearly publish the steps for requesting and obtaining a refund on their websites. The process should be simple, easy and accessible to any consumer. No one should go through unnecessary or complicated procedures i.e. sending the entire computer to a service centre just to remove unwanted software.
How to request your license refund
Start up the PC and take pictures
Take pictures of the screen of the clauses of the contract where the reimbursement is indicated or make a video by scrolling through the whole contract (maybe useful later). If possible, do not format/erase yet your computer storage.
Contact the manufacturer's customer service
Contact the manufacturer by telephone or, better still, chat/email, and keep the relevant correspondence. For the telephone, note the date, time and with whom you spoke. For chat, copy/paste what was written.
Problem Not Solved: fill-in the Refund Form and send it to the manufacturer.
Here you can find useful material to refund the cost of the Windows operating system.
Not all manufacturers and vendors are equal. Some react differently and treat consumers better. We have a lot of experience in requesting refunds, and keep track of those who respect your right to choose—and those who don't. Below we provide reports on manufacturers concerning their licenses and refund policies to help you in getting your money back.
HP does not have a reimbursement procedure for Windows.
Several contact attempts were made by different customers, and were always ignored by HP.
Lenovo has a reimbursement procedure for Windows.Lenovo license reimbursement procedure for Windows.
The PC must be shipped to a Lenovo assistance centre.
Asus has a reimbursement procedure for Windows.
No need to ship the PC to Asus.
Asus's reimbursement procedure is not published on their website.
Asus gives a reimbursement between 9 and 65 euros, depending on the Windows version.
Send an e-mail to info@asus.it indicating the PC serial number and your bank details, within 30 days of purchase and without accepting the EULA when you first turn on the machine.
Dell does not have a reimbursement procedure for Windows.
Dell's terms and conditions, in Article 7.3, explicitly states that in the event of non-approval of the operating system licence, the computer must be returned.
Acer has a reimbursement procedure for Windows. Acer license reimbursement procedure for Windows.
The PC must be shipped to an Acer assistance centre.
Forms to be filled in and submitted can be found on the Acer website.
Reports received. Get inspired. Explore information from other users like you who got their license fee back!
Following repeated unsuccessful telephone contacts, the ITfor company in Turin took Acer Italia to the Justice of the Peace contesting the manner in which the license was reimbursed. After several hearings and adjournments, Acer Italia granted payment of 50 euros + 100 euros for legal fees incurred.
After purchasing a Mediacom PC, Luca went directly to Datamatic S.p.A. (the parent company of the Mediacom brand) to request a refund of the Windows license. Only after the legal summons was served, and just before the legal hearing, Luca received an offer for a private transaction and awarded a refund of 44 euros.
Luca, after some perseverance, reached the Microsoft Technical Support of Microsoft S.r.l. (representing Microsoft in Italy), which actually provides a procedure for refunding the Windows license on products sold by the company (in this case, a Microsoft Surface). After several emails and communications, Luca received a refund of 43 euros.
Following a lengthy legal dispute, the judgment in the second instance awarded a refund of 42 euros for the Windows license, 1,000 for legal fees, and ordered Lenovo Italy S.r.l to reimburse 20,000 euros in damages for aggravated litigation liability.
The reimbursement request was denied several times, but the Justice of the Peace in Monza awarded a 61 euro reimbursement for pre-installed licenses (of both Windows 10 Home and Office 365 Personal).
After a couple of Italian legal emails (PEC emails), the 51 euro refund for the Windows 10 Home Edition license was granted.
After a long series of emails and phone calls, the 42 euro refund for the Windows 10 Home Edition license was granted. For the payment, Vincenzo chose to give Italian Linux Society's bank details.
After a particularly prolonged email exchange, a refund of 47 euros for the Windows 10 Home Edition license was granted.
Oggetto del contendere è stato - come in diversi altri casi - la presunta necessità di restituire il PC. Alla fine è stato riconosciuto un rimborso di 75 euro per la licenza Windows 11 Home.
Although Acer has a procedure for refunding the Windows license, it involves sending the PC, long waiting times and derisory compensation, so the procedure is inconvenient and impractical. The lengthy exchange of legal Italian emails (PEC emails) between Luca and Acer, culminating in the suggestion of a court case, ended in a 129 euro refund.
After many difficulties raised by MSI, including shipping the computer to the service center in Poland, long waiting times, and reminders, Giuseppe finally got a refund of 40 euros (net of shipping costs, absurdly charged to the customer).
It is recommended not to write to the email address for support, but to register on the MSI site and open a ticket specifying the serial number, first name, last name, mailing address, and phone number right away.
Get a licence free device
Want to buy a licence-free PC directly? Search for your nearest Linux-friendly shop on LinuxSi! (Italian-only).
My device is a smartphone. Check how you can install a different operating system on your smartphone FSFE's Free Your Android site.
The more people know, the stronger we are! Share this campaign with your friends, family, and on your social networks, by using #Refund4Freedom and #GetYourWindowsRefund.
Urge suppliers to express a clear position towards your rights.
Whether you got a refund or hit a roadblock, share your experience with others.					Tag @fsfe and @ItalianLinuxSociety on Mastodon and use our pre-made text for your social media posts.
If you asked for a refund, we can send to you some free stickers for your free laptop!
To receive news about the right to reimbursement of pre-installed software licences in Italy, see:							ADUC Windows refund page.

articles.title: Hundreds of migrants enter UK after 10-day lull
articles.summary: Nearly 500 people crossed the Channel in seven boats on Thursday - the first since 17 August.
articles.body:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, An inflatable small boat pictured in April 2026Nearly 500 migrants have arrived in the UK in one day, in the first boats to successfully cross the Channel in 10 days.The seven vessels that made the crossing were the first since 17 August when 250 people arrived.Dinghies arrived in British waters until late into the night on Thursday, with 494 people being brought into the Border Security Command compound in Dover, Kent.The total number is down overall this year, according to BBC Verify analysis of government data.
How many people cross the English Channel in small boats?
Between 1 January and 27 August 2026, a total of 16,391 people crossed the English Channel by small boat from France. This was down by 43% on the same period the previous year.
These crossings have become the most common way for people to be detected entering the UK illegally since 2020.
Nearly all those who arrive by small boat claim asylum. Under international law, this means they are allowed to stay in the country while their asylum application is considered.
Small boat arrivals made up 40% of asylum applications between July 2025 to June 2026.
Boats that arrived in the UK from 28 August 2025 to 27 August 2026 carried an average of 68 people. This has more than doubled since 2021.
Experts say overcrowding in boats makes crossings riskier. At least 84 people died while attempting to cross the Channel in 2024, according to the United Nations (UN).
When looking at the scale of small boats crossings, the number of these arrivals is about 5% of the size of total immigration into the UK from January 2025 to December 2025.
The government has pledged to “smash the gangs” behind these crossings in order to reduce the numbers.
Who is arriving in the UK on small boats?
People from Eritrea accounted for 18% of all arrivals from July 2025 to June 2026.
In the latest figures covering January 2025 to December 2025, at least 2,335 people who arrived by small boat were found to be potential victims of human trafficking or other forms of modern slavery, according to the Home Office.
How else do people stay in the UK without permission?
Another 4,712 people were detected entering the UK without permission via other methods including hiding in vehicles, travelling on ferries or through airports from July 2025 to June 2026. This was down by 17% on the same period the previous year.
There are also individuals who arrive legally, for example via a work or study visa, and then overstay their limit.
The total number of people who live in the UK illegally after arriving legally is not known.
Some 16,391 migrants have crossed the Channel so far, down 43% on the same time last year, and a 17% drop from the same point in 2024.Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has said she will not be "complacent" about the falling numbers, and that there is "more we must do"."That is why I have boosted enforcement on the French beaches and overseas and introduced new legislation to tackle the pull factors that draw people here through unsafe and illegal routes," she added.Follow BBC Kent on Facebook,, external X, external and on Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds. Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk, external or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250.More on this storyRelated internet links

articles.title: Htmx 4.0
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://four.htmx.org/announcements/2026-08-28-htmx-4.0.0-is-released

Points: 786

articles.body:
The htmx team is very happy to announce the release of htmx 4.0.0!  This is the culmination of 8 months of work (plus
a game) and we are very happy with the results.
The idea of htmx 4 started to germinate when I decided to create fixi and, in doing so, got
more familiar with the fetch() API and async programming in JavaScript.  (htmx had always
One chance evening I was contacted by Christian, who had some interesting ideas
got me thinking that moving the internals to fetch() would simplify things for him and for the library in general.
After a bit of work I managed to get Michael and Alex on board, and we were off to the races.
Development has been very smooth. We started a port of fixi + the htmx test suite. Over time, we rediscovered why htmx
did many of the things that it did and moved our new implementation closer and closer to the old one. At this point
the behavioral differences between 2.x and 4.x are relatively small and where they do diverge we have made explicit
choices that we feel will put htmx-based applications in a good spot for
Note that we are not marking 4.0 as latest in NPM
because we do not want to force-upgrade users who are relying on non-versioned CDN URLs for htmx. Instead, 2.x will
remain latest and the 4.0 line will remain next until some point in early 2027. The website, however, will reference 4.0.
As mentioned above, htmx 4, from a user’s viewpoint, is almost identical to htmx 2. There are three major changes:
Attribute inheritance is now explicit by default rather than implicit by default (this is the biggest upgrade item)
The htmx event names have been standardized & cleaned up. Some advanced users may need to change the events they
History support now does not use localStorage by default (which was a cause of many support headaches). Most people
won’t notice this at all.
Internally, we migrated from XMLHttpRequest to fetch() but that should be transparent for most users of htmx.
In htmx 2 many attributes were “inherited” by default. This allows you to place attributes on parent elements and
their behavior will apply to child elements. This behavior, which came from
the intercooler.js days, was inspired by CSS and, unsurprisingly, worked out about the same
as CSS: powerful but difficult to understand at times.
In htmx 4 attributes are not inherited unless you explicitly say so by adding an
:inherited after the attribute name:
This will be the largest upgrade burden in migrating from htmx 2 to htmx 4. To make things easier, we have provided
a command line tool to find places you need to mark as inherited.
Note that attributes like hx-disinherit, etc. are no longer required and should be removed.
The events triggered by htmx 2 had grown organically over the life of the library and were not particularly well
organized, making it difficult to know exactly which event was fired when.
In htmx 4, all events now follow htmx:phase:action[:sub-action]:
In addition, the following changes were made:
Most error events collapse into htmx:error. HTTP error responses fire
The htmx:xhr:* events are removed. htmx 4 uses fetch().
The htmx:validation:* events are removed in favor of native browser form validation.
The full table is in What’s New in htmx 4.
The command line upgrade checker flags old event names in hx-on attributes and in your JavaScript where it can find
History support has always been included in htmx, allowing you to implement back-button aware actions with simple
attributes. In htmx 2, a cache in localStorage was used to snapshot pages for restoration. Unfortunately a large
source of issues was that this snapshot could include DOM mutations by 3rd party JavaScript libraries. When the page was
restored, those mutations remained but the underlying JavaScript logic was not.
htmx 4 does not cache pages in localStorage. On back navigation htmx re-fetches the page and swaps it into <body>,
or into the [hx-history-elt] element if one is present. This allows 3rd party JavaScript libraries to “just work” in
most cases and, with good request caching, is very fast.
If you want local caching instead, we now ship a very complete hx-history-cache
extension that restores history from sessionStorage and is designed to integrate well with scripting solutions like
There are two big new features in htmx 4, both of which we are really excited about:
We now support morphing swaps out of the box with htmx.  I created idiomorph and
nearly included it in htmx 2.x but decided against it.  In htmx 4, Michael has done great work improving on that
algorithm and integrating it seamlessly into htmx.
Another major new feature is the <hx-partial> tag.  This tag is similar to out-of-band swaps,
but is much clearer when you want to do something beyond just replacing a single element with a new version of itself:
Much of the excitement in htmx 4 is in the extensions.  Switching to fetch() internally let us rethink how extensions
can and should work, and sparked the creation (and recreation) of many new extensions, for example:
hx-preload - preload content (e.g. on mouseover) to speed requests up
hx-download - native, fetch-based file downloads
hx-alpine-compat - smooths over compatibility issues between htmx and Alpine.js
hx-history-cache - caches history in sessionStorage, provides Alpine.js compatibility
Additionally, there are three new or updated streaming HTML extensions:
hx-ws streams and sends over WebSockets.
Finally, we decided it was time to try our hand at our own small front-end scripting solution that tightly integrates with htmx.  hx-live is inspired by Alpine.js, jQuery and hyperscript, and makes front end scripting pleasant and fun.  It even supports what we are calling DOM-based, HATEOAS-friendly reactivity.
There is a new htmax.js bundle in the distribution which packages htmx with the most popular of these in a single file if you don’t want to think about which ones you want to pick.
For a complete upgrade guide see  What’s New in htmx 4.
As mentioned earlier, we are providing an upgrade tool to help you:
$ npx htmx.org@4.0.0 upgrade-check -- ./templates
File extensions: .html, .php, .js, .ts, .jinja, .jinja2, .j2, .erb, .hbs
Use --ext to add more (e.g. --ext .vue --ext .svelte)
Found 8 issue(s) in 1 of 1 file(s).
templates/index.html:1: [inheritance] hx-headers needs :inherited suffix (descendant on line 3 has hx-delete) (this looks like a CSRF token; without :inherited the header does not reach child elements and the server rejects the request)
templates/index.html:2: [inheritance] hx-target needs :inherited suffix (descendant on line 3 has hx-delete)
templates/index.html:2: [inheritance] hx-confirm needs :inherited suffix (descendant on line 3 has hx-delete)
templates/index.html:3: [renamed-attr] hx-disable -> rename to hx-ignore (hx-disable now means 'disable during request')
templates/index.html:4: [removed-attr] hx-vars is removed -> use hx-vals with js: prefix
templates/index.html:4: [removed-attr] hx-prompt is removed -> load the hx-prompt extension to keep the same syntax
templates/index.html:9: [old-event] old event name "htmx:afterRequest" -> "htmx:after:request"
templates/index.html:9: [old-api] htmx.addClass() is removed -> use element.classList.add()
We are also shipping an agent skill to assist in upgrading
htmx 4.0 can be installed via a package manager referencing version 4.0.0, or can be linked via a CDN:
Like it or not, a lot of people are using LLMs and we are providing the following skills files for LLMs:
htmx-guidance - core htmx skills for developing with htmx 4
htmx-debugging - diagnosing htmx issues during dev
htmx-extension-authoring - writing and debugging htmx 4 extensions
htmx-upgrade-from-htmx2 - migrating a codebase from htmx 2.x to 4.x
(Let’s leave aside if releasing a new version of a library in the LLM era is a good or bad thing!)
We hope you enjoy htmx 4.  htmx 2 will continue to be supported indefinitely so don’t feel any pressure to upgrade.
I’d like to thank the following people for all their help with this release:
Michael West - Incredible teammate & grug-brained developer
Christian Tanul - Inspired htmx 4 & led the streaming & live extensions
Alex Petros - For keeping the ship on an even keel
Stephen Mitchell - The genius behind the game
Stu Kennedy - Our WebSockets expert
André Ahlert Jr. - Providing IDE & Editor Support
Dien Hoa Truong - For kicking the tires on early htmx 4 and helping fix many bugs

articles.title: a16z creates a $1.1B ‘Machine Age’ fund to ‘accelerate the physical buildout of AI’
articles.summary: The firm, known for its focus on software, is going to start throwing more money at the hardware behind AI.
articles.body:
Andreessen Horowitz has launched a new “Machine Age” fund with $1.1 billion raised. The firm’s aim with the new fund is to “open the throttle and accelerate the physical buildout of AI.”
The fund will focus on hardware, bucking the firm’s typical focus on the scaling power of software. In a post on the venture capital firm’s website, a16z says the fund will focus on investing in the infrastructure that powers AI — a swath that includes everything from computer chips and memory to data centers and robots.
“We need faster, more efficient systems. We need cheaper and higher-bandwidth memory across the memory hierarchy. We need faster and more scalable interconnects between nodes and systems. We need power efficient edge devices for AI to explore and interact with the world. And of course we need all the cooling, materials, electrical, and real estate build out to support them,” the post reads.
AI is the “strongest tool ever developed for solving problems and bestowing abundance,” the firm writes, calling its advancement a “social and national imperative.”
articles.author: Sean O'Kane

articles.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.
articles.body:
A federal judge in California ruled on Thursday evening that the Trump administration’s designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk was illegal.
U.S. District Judge Rita Lin said in her ruling that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s labeling of Anthropic as a risk to national security signified “unlawful retaliation” in violation of the First Amendment, and said the decision was “arbitrary and capricious.” Lin also said Anthropic was denied due process, as required under the Fifth Amendment.
Earlier this year, Hegseth and President Donald Trump labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk and ordered all federal agencies, even those outside of defense, to stop working with the Claude maker.
The dispute stemmed from Anthropic setting hard lines on certain safety guardrails that would allow the Pentagon to use its models for fully autonomous weapons and mass surveillance of American citizens. The Pentagon denied that it would use Anthropic models for anything but lawful purposes, and alleged that Anthropic could try to control the military’s use of the models it bought and paid for.
In her ruling, Lin said that the government’s “words and deeds confirm that the challenged actions were based on a desire to make a public example out of Anthropic for its ‘arrogance’ in criticizing the government.”
She pointed out the disconnect between the supply-chain label and other actions from the government, like Hegseth’s proposition to apply the Defense Production Act to Anthropic, “which would mean the company was essential to national security rather than a threat to it.” She also pointed to the Department of Defense continuing to pursue a contract with the company, and the government collaborating with the company’s new model, Mythos, for cybersecurity.
Lin also said it’s clear that Anthropic “undisputedly lacks” any backdoor access to its technology once it hands it over to the DOD.
“Though the Department of War is undisputedly free to select the AI vendor of its choice, the evidence demonstrates that the broad measures imposed on Anthropic were illegal and baseless,” Lin wrote. “The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,” she added.
“We welcome the court’s ruling that this supply chain risk designation was unlawful,” an Anthropic spokesperson said in a statement shared with TechCrunch. “We remain focused on working productively with the government to harness AI for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology.”
Anthropic filed two complaints against the DOD in March in California and Washington, D.C. The D.C. suit is still ongoing.
TechCrunch has reached out to the DOD for comment.

articles.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
articles.summary: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.
articles.body:
Meta’s India and Southeast Asia vice president, Sandhya Devanathan, is leaving the social media giant to join OpenAI, the ChatGPT maker told TechCrunch.
Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to OpenAI’s Asia-Pacific managing director, Kiran Mani. She will oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement, and operations across Southeast Asia and Australia, OpenAI said.
The executive is leaving Meta after more than a decade at the company, which has been the subject of growing scrutiny over issues such as online safety and content moderation. Devanathan was involved in the company’s decision process in the country, a person familiar with the matter said.
Devanathan’s appointment comes days after Prabhjeet Singh joined OpenAI as its India head. Singh had spent more than a decade at Uber, where he led its India and South Asia business.
OpenAI has been expanding its presence across the Asia Pacific, opening offices in Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney, and Delhi over the past two years.
Following Devanathan’s departure, Meta’s India managing director, Arun Srinivas, will report directly to Benjamin Joe, the company’s vice president for Asia Pacific, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch.
Devanathan joined Meta in 2016 and held several leadership roles at the company, including leading its Asia Pacific gaming business, before being appointed vice president for India and Southeast Asia in June last year.
Meta has faced growing pressure from Indian authorities in recent weeks. Earlier this month, the company apologized after Instagram mistakenly restricted a post by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July. The Indian government summoned Meta executives, including its chief global affairs officer, Joel Kaplan, over the incident.

articles.title: Apple TV’s sci-fi thriller Dark Matter gets even trippier in season 2
articles.summary: Confusion is a generally accepted side effect of mystery box shows. They slather on secrets with the promise of a satisfying payoff in the end, and sometimes the cast and crew even have a hard time following what's going on. But even by the standards of the genre, Dark Matter is extreme. Its multiversal premise, which involves a man kidnapping a version of himself from another world, can be hard t
articles.body:
Confusion is a generally accepted side effect of mystery box shows. They slather on secrets with the promise of a satisfying payoff in the end, and sometimes the cast and crew even have a hard time following what’s going on. But even by the standards of the genre, Dark Matter is extreme. Its multiversal premise, which involves a man kidnapping a version of himself from another world, can be hard to wrap your head around, and as the first season went on, things only got harder to follow. With the return of the show for season 2, I have both good and bad news: The show is more dramatic and thrilling than ever, while also being ever so much harder to follow.
Spoilers follow for the first season of Dark Matter.
First, a reminder of where the story left us. Based on the novel of the same name, Dark Matter follows Jason Dessen (Joel Edgerton), a physics professor in Chicago who is living a relatively normal and contented life with his artist wife Daniela (Jennifer Connelly) and teenage son Charlie (Oakes Fegley). In another world, a different version of Jason decided to forgo that family life in pursuit of his dream, which was apparently to build a gigantic box that allowed people to travel to other parallel universes. But that alt version of Jason ultimately wasn’t satisfied with the life he had, and used the box to travel to a world where he and Daniela were together. He then kidnapped himself, abandoned that version in another world, and proceeded to take over his life.
Things did not go as planned for alt Jason. Daniela eventually realized that something was wrong, Jason prime fought his way through multiple worlds to get back home, and by the end of the season, an army of Jason variants had descended on the same version of Chicago in hopes of reuniting with Daniela. At the end of the finale, the original Jason, Daniela, and Charlie had made their way into the box in hopes of finding a new world where they could live out a normal life in peace.
Still with me? Well, good, because things only get more complex from here. Dark Matter is obviously a high-concept sci-fi thriller, but in season 2, it really pushes further into its premise, exploring all of the wild possibilities. Jason and his family are living like multiversal nomads, traveling to different worlds in search of a home, and this lets the show get into the nitty-gritty of how the box works and the rules for traveling between worlds. It’s an inexact science: You can’t just go wherever you want. Instead, your destination is dependent on your mindset when you open the door. So if you’re scared or stressed out, get ready for a postapocalyptic version of Chicago.
This premise leads to some really great moments. The Dessens, for instance, are going through a situation that no family has ever gone through, which puts all kinds of strain on their relationships. But the show is often at its best when it moves away from the main story. One episode explores several years in the life of a random Jason variant who simply tries to build a life for himself in a quiet world. It’s a melancholy short story that reminds me of the “Long, Long Time” episode of The Last of Us. It doesn’t try to push the story forward or inundate you with revelations; instead, it shows you the human impact of this technology. There’s a similar episode that introduces a sort of waystation that various multiverse travelers visit over the years, and one that involves Charlie seeking out a long-lost family member in another world.
But getting to these moments means being okay with being confused, and that’s because season 2 really ratchets up the complexity primarily by introducing a whole bunch of new characters, most of whom are variants of existing ones. That means a lot of Jasons, Danielas, and Charlies, of course — the original alt Jason who started this mess features prominently — but also their friends and coworkers like chemist Ryan (Jimmi Simpson), psychologist Amanda (Alice Braga), and the well-off Leighton (Dayo Okeniyi) who is bankrolling the whole thing. There are multiple versions of each, spread across different worlds, all of which are involved to some degree in the larger story. It’s a lot to keep track of, and the show often doesn’t help much in differentiating the variants so that it’s clear who you’re actually watching. At one point, the main Jason and Daniela get tattoos so they can clearly identify each other. On top of this, season 2 jumps around in time quite a bit, further putting a strain on your ability to follow narrative threads.
That kind of knotty storytelling is perhaps unavoidable with a premise as convoluted as Dark Matter’s, but season 2 shows that series can also do a lot when it slows down and explores human-level stories, as opposed to racing toward the next big set piece. The second season attempts to balance both kinds of storytelling — it even ends with what feels like some Christopher Nolan–inspired action — which means that in order to experience the show at its best, you’ll have to resign yourself to not understanding everything.
Dark Matter season 2 is streaming on Apple TV on August 28th.
articles.author: Andrew Webster

articles.title: Migrating to HTTPX2
articles.summary:
Article URL: https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/httpx2.md
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49477212
Points: 198
# Comments: 89
articles.body:
The OpenAI Python SDK now uses HTTPX2 for its
synchronous and asynchronous HTTP clients. HTTPX2 is installed automatically
with openai; the previous httpx package is not. This guide explains what
changes for applications that interact with the SDK's HTTP layer.
If you use the SDK's default HTTP client
If you construct an OpenAI or
AsyncOpenAI client without providing http_client, your existing API calls,
parsed response models, streaming APIs, authentication, retries, and numeric
No HTTPX2 extra or separate installation is required:
If your application imported httpx only because an earlier SDK installed it
transitively, add your own httpx dependency or migrate those imports to
httpx2. Installing the SDK no longer installs httpx for you.
TLS certificates and trust stores
HTTPX2 changes the default TLS trust store, including for applications that
use the SDK's default HTTP client. HTTPX previously verified certificates
against the CA bundle provided by certifi. HTTPX2 instead uses the
operating-system trust store, and the SDK no longer installs certifi.
This can break certificate verification in minimal container images without
system CA certificates, environments using corporate TLS-inspecting proxies,
and deployments that relied on a custom or modified certifi bundle. Install
the required CA certificates in the operating-system trust store, or configure
Alternatively, configure a directory of trusted CA certificates:
These environment variables are honored when trust_env=True, which is the
default. To control trust explicitly on a custom client, pass an
from openai import OpenAI, DefaultHttpx2Client
Use DefaultAsyncHttpx2Client(verify=ssl_context) for the equivalent async
configuration. The SDK's aiohttp transport uses the same HTTPX2 TLS settings.
If you provide a custom HTTP client
Use HTTPX2 clients and HTTPX2 configuration objects. The SDK provides helpers
that preserve its recommended timeout, connection-pool, and redirect defaults:
from openai import OpenAI, AsyncOpenAI, DefaultHttpx2Client, DefaultAsyncHttpx2Client
Directly constructed httpx2.Client and httpx2.AsyncClient instances are
also supported. When you construct a client directly, its own HTTPX2 defaults
apply unless you configure them yourself.
The existing DefaultHttpxClient and DefaultAsyncHttpxClient names continue
to work, but now construct HTTPX2 clients. Prefer DefaultHttpx2Client and
DefaultAsyncHttpx2Client when making the HTTP client family explicit.
Module-level configuration follows the same rule:
Timeouts, URLs, transports, and connection settings
Replace HTTPX-specific objects with the corresponding HTTPX2 objects:
For example, a granular SDK timeout becomes:
client = OpenAI(timeout=httpx2.Timeout(60.0, connect=5.0, read=20.0))
Numeric timeout values do not change. Existing string URLs do not change.
Custom transport subclasses, mounted transports, proxy integrations, and
connection-pool instrumentation must target HTTPX2's transport interfaces.
Authentication handlers and hooks receive HTTPX2 request and response objects.
Update custom auth classes and annotations accordingly:
from openai import OpenAI, DefaultHttpx2Client
def log_request(request: httpx2.Request) -> None:
If you subclass an HTTP authentication or transport interface, subclass the
matching httpx2 class. Third-party instrumentation, tracing middleware, and
auth integrations must explicitly support HTTPX2.
Raw responses, streaming, and exceptions
Parsed SDK response models are unchanged. When using a native HTTPX2 client,
transport-facing objects belong to HTTPX2:
With a native client, use cast_to=httpx2.Response when requesting an unparsed
HTTP response. Streaming response wrappers also expose HTTPX2 response objects.
Application code should usually catch SDK exceptions such as
openai.APITimeoutError and openai.APIConnectionError; with a native client,
an exception's underlying transport cause is an HTTPX2 exception.
These type guarantees apply only to native HTTPX2 clients. An injected legacy
HTTPX client produces httpx.Request, httpx.Response, and HTTPX transport
exceptions instead, even if cast_to=httpx2.Response is supplied.
The supported aiohttp extra uses an HTTPX2-native transport. It does not
install legacy HTTPX or the external httpx-aiohttp adapter:
from openai import AsyncOpenAI, DefaultAioHttpClient
DefaultAioHttpClient() is an httpx2.AsyncClient. Applications using this
helper do not need to construct or import the transport directly.
Mocks must intercept HTTPX2 requests and return HTTPX2 responses. For example:
def handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
If your test suite uses RESPX, update to an HTTPX2-compatible RESPX version or
fork. A RESPX version that patches only legacy HTTPX cannot intercept the SDK's
default HTTPX2 client. If you cannot migrate that integration immediately, the
temporary legacy-client escape hatch below lets existing HTTPX-only RESPX
setups continue to work while you migrate.
Temporary escape hatch: a legacy HTTPX client
Applications that depend on an HTTPX-only transport, integration, or mocking
library can explicitly install legacy HTTPX and inject a legacy client:
Legacy HTTPX support is runtime-only. The SDK's public type annotations
accept HTTPX2 clients, so passing a legacy client directly fails static type
checking in mypy, Pyright, and similar tools. Use cast(Any, ...) or a
targeted type-ignore when deliberately choosing this compatibility path:
from typing import Any, cast
The asynchronous form requires the same workaround:
from typing import Any, cast
Legacy clients preserve the HTTPX request, response, and exception families.
Request raw responses as httpx.Response, using the same type-checking
workaround for the legacy response class:
from typing import Any, cast
response = client.get("/models", cast_to=cast(Any, httpx.Response))
Passing cast_to=httpx2.Response does not convert a legacy HTTPX response into
an HTTPX2 response. Install and maintain the legacy dependency yourself.
Legacy HTTPX support is provided as a migration aid and may be discontinued.
If you must retain an existing httpx-aiohttp integration, install it
explicitly and inject its legacy client:
from typing import Any, cast
This path is covered by dedicated compatibility tests, including a real
request through the aiohttp transport, but remains a temporary escape hatch.
Prefer openai[aiohttp] and DefaultAioHttpClient() for new code.
